<!-- diagram:nereus-api:end -->

*Clients hold a token, never a kubeconfig; what is behind the door stays behind it.*

## How it works

- It runs in the cluster as `nereus-api` in `nereus-system`, installed by `nereus init` with core; its public name is `api.<domain>`.
- It alone validates the token: the issuer and keys come from the authentication Reef's default Mandate, the audience is `nereus-api`, and the Kubernetes apiserver never sees a person's token.
- It acts with its own identity, and decides what the person may do before acting ([Tenancy and access](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/tenancy-and-access/)).
- It speaks of Reefs and their kinds, never of tools, and reads what the Nereids publish in `status`; what it did not read, it says it did not.
- Command groups move behind it one at a time; the rest keep the kubeconfig as a stand-in, and the check `kubeconfig-ban` refuses any new use outside `nereus init` and the bootstrap.

## Not this

- Not the Kubernetes API: the Reefs' kinds live there, but no client reaches it directly.
- Not a proxy to each tool's API: no route names Flux, Keycloak or OpenBao.
- Not the portal: the portal is one client of the API, as the CLI is.

## Next

[Install the CLI](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/install/): try it on your own machine.

# Keep the CLI up to date

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/cli-update.md

Keep a `nereus` installed from a release up to date: it upgrades itself in the background, and you choose how ([#1782](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1782)).

## Before you start

- `nereus` installed from a release, as in [Install the CLI](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/install/). An editable install from a checkout updates with `git pull` instead: [Run the CLI from a checkout](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/build/cli-checkout/).

## Steps

### 1. Let it upgrade itself

At most once a day, a call starts `nereus upgrade --background` on its own, detached, and the next call says so on stderr:

``` { .text .output title="output" }
nereus upgraded 0.1.22 → 0.1.23
```

The worker reads the release manifest (`latest.json` of the `getnereus/install` releases), refuses a wheel whose sha256 differs, and installs it with `uv tool install --force`. It logs to `~/.local/state/nereus/upgrade.log` (`$XDG_STATE_HOME`).

### 2. Upgrade now, or only look

```bash
nereus upgrade
```

`nereus upgrade --check` only says which release is the latest.

### 3. Choose how it upgrades

The CLI's config, `~/.config/nereus/config.yaml`, holds the mode: `background` installs (the default), `notify` only says that a release is available, `off` never looks.

```bash
nereus config set auto_upgrade notify
```

`nereus config set check_interval 7d` looks once a week. For one shell, `NEREUS_AUTO_UPGRADE=off` wins over the config.

## Check it worked

`nereus --version` prints the release you upgraded to. It never upgrades on its own an editable install, a dev version (`0.1.23.dev4`), a run with `CI` set, or shell completion.

## Next

[Write the settings](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/settings/) of an installation, or [prepare a cluster for Nereus](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/cluster/).

## Learn more

- `NEREUS_VERSION=0.1.23` pins a version at install time; `sh -s -- --help` lists the installer's options.
- [The settings file](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/settings/) holds the settings of `nereus init`, not the CLI's own config.

# Prepare a cluster for Nereus

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/cluster.md

Make a cluster that offers what Nereus needs, by hand, for [Install with Helm](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/helm/); `nereus init --create-cluster` does the same for you.

## Before you start

What any cluster must offer, and how k3d and AKS meet it. AKS is there to compare and is **not tested**: no installation has run on it yet.

| Need | k3d | AKS (not tested) |
|---|---|---|
| Tools | Docker 20.10.5+, k3d 5.0.0+, Helm 4.0.0+ | `az`, Helm 4.0.0+ |
| Host | `fs.inotify.max_user_instances=1024` | the nodes are Azure's |
| Entrance: Gateway API kinds, a way to the Gateway | no Traefik; `127.0.0.1:8080` to the load balancer's port 80 | a `LoadBalancer` Service with a public IP, DNS and TLS in front |
| Images | the local registry, or `ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus` | `ghcr.io`, or a copy in an Azure Container Registry |
| Registry trust: every node trusts the local registry's CA | the CA's certificate mounted on every node | not needed: the nodes pull from a container registry such as ACR or `ghcr.io`, with credentials |
| The [registry Reef](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/registry/): a registry in the cluster | its CA is the one of step 2, which every node trusts | [planned]: the nodes would have to trust its CA |
| API server: anonymous reads of the issuer's discovery only | an `AuthenticationConfiguration` on the server | `--enable-oidc-issuer`; the anonymous read is still to check |

On a machine that already has a k3d cluster named `nereus`, such as one kept for daily work, pick another name and port: replace `nereus` in the commands of step 5 and Clean up, and `8080` in `--port`.
| Storage: a default StorageClass | `local-path` | `managed-csi` |
| Network: NetworkPolicy enforced | k3s enforces it | `--network-policy azure`, `calico` or `cilium` |

## Steps

The steps make a k3d cluster; the registry CA of steps 2 and 3 is for its local registry. AKS follows after step 5.

### 1. Raise the host's inotify limit

With Ubuntu's default of 128, a second k3d cluster never starts. Raise it once per machine.

```bash
echo "fs.inotify.max_user_instances=1024" \
  | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-k3d-inotify.conf
sudo sysctl --system
```

### 2. Make the registry CA

A Registry answers only over TLS, with a certificate from one CA every node trusts. Its name constraints allow only `localhost` and names under `svc.cluster.local`, so trusting it trusts nothing else. Keep its files in a folder of your own, `nereus/`.

```bash
mkdir --parents nereus/registry
(umask 077 && openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out nereus/ca.key)
openssl req -new -x509 -sha256 -days 3650 \
  -key nereus/ca.key \
  -out nereus/registry/ca.crt \
  -subj "/CN=Nereus registry CA" \
  -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:true,pathlen:0" \
  -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" \
  -addext "nameConstraints=critical,permitted;DNS:localhost,permitted;DNS:svc.cluster.local,excluded;IP:0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0,excluded;IP:::/::"
chmod 0755 nereus nereus/registry
chmod 0644 nereus/registry/ca.crt
```

### 3. Trust it for every registry

`nereus/registries.yaml` adds the CA to the roots of every registry the nodes pull from.

```yaml
configs:
  "*":
    tls:
      ca_file: /etc/nereus/registry/ca.crt
```

### 4. Open the issuer's discovery

zot reads the cluster issuer's discovery and keys with no token, to check a build's push token. k3s turns anonymous requests off; `nereus/authentication-config.yaml` lets them in on those two paths only.

```yaml
apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: AuthenticationConfiguration
anonymous:
  enabled: true
  conditions:
    - path: /.well-known/openid-configuration
    - path: /openid/v1/jwks
```

### 5. Create the cluster

No load balancer, since k3d's is nginx, and the API on the loopback only (#2152); no Traefik, since the profile brings Istio's Gateway; the Gateway on port 8080 of the loopback; the CA on every node and the configuration on the server. Docker mounts absolute paths.

```bash
k3d cluster create nereus \
  --no-lb \
  --api-port "127.0.0.1:random" \
  --k3s-arg "--disable=traefik@server:*" \
  --port "127.0.0.1:8080:80@server:0:direct" \
  --registry-config nereus/registries.yaml \
  --volume "${PWD}/nereus/registry:/etc/nereus/registry@all" \
  --volume "${PWD}/nereus/authentication-config.yaml:/etc/rancher/nereus/authentication-config.yaml@server:*" \
  --k3s-arg "--kube-apiserver-arg=authentication-config=/etc/rancher/nereus/authentication-config.yaml@server:*" \
  --wait
```

Keep `nereus/`: the nodes mount it, the API server reads its file on every restart, and the chart `nereus` takes the CA from it.

On AKS, the same rows are flags of `az aks create`: `--network-plugin azure --network-policy azure`, `--enable-oidc-issuer` and `--enable-workload-identity`; a build pool is a node pool labelled and tainted `build.getnereus.dev/pool=build`.

## Check it worked

`kubectl get storageclass` shows `local-path` as the default, and `kubectl get nodes` shows every node Ready. After the install, [`nereus doctor`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#doctor) says when the issuer's discovery is closed.

## Clean up

Delete the cluster with `k3d cluster delete nereus` and its folder with `rm -r nereus`.

## Next

- [Install with Helm](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/helm/) on this cluster.

## Learn more

- [Runtime and profiles](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/runtime-and-profiles/): what the profile installs on the cluster.

# Install with Helm

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/helm.md

Install Nereus and the profile `internal-developer-platform` on a cluster you made, with two `helm upgrade --install` lines and no `nereus init`.

## Before you start

- The k3d cluster `nereus` of [Prepare a cluster for Nereus](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/cluster/), with its folder `nereus/` kept: the nodes mount it, and the chart `nereus` takes the registry CA from it.
- `helm` and `kubectl` pointed at that cluster. Both charts and every image are published on `ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus`, by digest, so nothing is built.

## Steps

### 1. Install the kinds

The chart `nereus-reefs` holds every kind, kept on uninstall, so a plain `helm upgrade` updates them.

```bash
helm upgrade --install nereus-reefs \
  oci://ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus-reefs \
  --version 0.1.6 \
  --namespace nereus-system \
  --create-namespace \
  --wait
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Release "nereus-reefs" does not exist. Installing it now.
Pulled: ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus-reefs:0.1.6
Digest: sha256:50389e42b8f2ed45423ca3c221607cc28aa1984c411c528912ec18daa5ac8246
NAME: nereus-reefs
NAMESPACE: nereus-system
STATUS: deployed
REVISION: 1
DESCRIPTION: Install complete
```

### 2. Install the Gateway API's kinds

The chart `nereus` renders the API's route only when the Gateway API's kinds exist, so apply them first, at the version `nereus init` uses.

```bash
kubectl apply --server-side --filename \
  https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.7.0/standard-install.yaml
```

### 3. Install Nereus and the profile

The chart `nereus` brings the API and thetis, the installer Nereid, plus the Installation, the Profile and the registry CA as the Secret `registry-ca`. `--take-ownership` adopts the namespace of step 1.

```bash
helm upgrade --install nereus oci://ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus \
  --version 0.1.6 \
  --namespace nereus-system \
  --take-ownership \
  --set installation.name=nereus \
  --set profile=internal-developer-platform \
  --set ingress.address=http://localhost:8080 \
  --set-file registryCA.certificate=nereus/registry/ca.crt \
  --set-file registryCA.key=nereus/ca.key
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Release "nereus" does not exist. Installing it now.
Pulled: ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus:0.1.6
Digest: sha256:2beceb8078d35e6ac4ebc90a0ba4cdd0bd873664794336fd22f5d953920e9a7f
NAME: nereus
NAMESPACE: nereus-system
STATUS: deployed
REVISION: 1
DESCRIPTION: Install complete
```

The profile is the file `profiles/<profile>.yaml` of the chart; a name with no file fails before anything is installed, listing the profiles there are.

The metrics Reef scrapes every 30s; `--set metrics.scrapeInterval=15s` changes it, whole seconds from 10s to 60s, before thetis creates the metrics Reef's Mandate ([#2199](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/2199)). Any other value fails the chart.

### 4. Remove the CA key

The key now lives in the Secret, kept on uninstall, and in Helm's release history in `nereus-system`. Delete the file with `rm nereus/ca.key`.

### 5. Wait for the profile

thetis installs each Reef, Nereid and Mandate in the order of what each requires; the Profile is Ready when the last one is, in about 8 minutes.

```bash
kubectl get profiles.core.getnereus.dev nereus --watch
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME     PROFILE                       READY   AGE
nereus   internal-developer-platform   True    8m30s
```

### 6. Log in

Helm writes no CLI config: set `NEREUS_API_URL=http://localhost:8080` so every command finds the instance, then [`nereus login`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#login-device) keeps that URL.

```bash
nereus login --use-device-code
```

## Check it worked

[`nereus reef list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#reef-list) shows the same Reefs `nereus init --profile internal-developer-platform` gives; `nereus nereid list` shows each Nereid Ready, from `ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus`.

```bash
nereus reef list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
REEF            NEREIDS
authentication  keycloak
build           buildkit
catalog         catalog
database        cloudnative-pg
delivery        kubernetes
environment     vcluster
metrics         victoriametrics
portal          nereus-portal
registry        zot
release         flux
scm             forgejo
secrets         openbao
tenancy         -
```

## Clean up

Delete the cluster with `k3d cluster delete nereus` and its folder with `rm -r nereus`.

## Next

- [Rebuild the kept cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/kept-cluster/) from a published version.
- [Keep a secret](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/secrets/) in the vault the profile made.

## Learn more

- [Runtime and profiles](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/runtime-and-profiles/): what a profile installs and in what order.

# Deploy main to the live cluster

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/deploy-live.md

Upgrade the `live` cluster in place to the commit of `main`, from the published charts, and check it with the smoke test.

## Before you start

- `live` is today the kept cluster `k3d-nereus` (see [Rebuild the kept cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/kept-cluster/)). The scenes use it too, so the script refuses it without `--allow-kept-cluster`, and the other sessions on the repository are asked first.
- A clone of the repository: the script runs on your machine, by hand; no GitHub Action is involved, and the trigger on every push comes later (#914).
- `NEREUS_LIVE_CONTEXT=k3d-nereus` exported, the kubeconfig context the script uses; `kubectl --context k3d-nereus get nodes` answers.

## Steps

### 1. See the plan

A dry run prints every command, resolves the commit of `main` and touches nothing.

```bash
scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster --dry-run
```

### 2. Deploy and test

The script fetches `origin/main`, runs `helm upgrade --install` for `nereus-reefs`, then `nereus`, from `oci://ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts`, records the commit as the annotation `deploy.getnereus.dev/commit` on `nereus-system`, then runs the smoke test. The first run on a cluster names the installation, which never changes after that.

```bash
scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster --installation-name nereus
```

A failed upgrade ends the run before the commit is recorded. Each upgrade runs with `--force-conflicts`: on `live`, the chart decides over a field another manager changed.

### 3. Drop values the chart owns now

A release installed by hand or by `nereus init` may hold values such as an `image` pointing at the local registry. `--reset-values` drops them, so the chart's published images, by digest, apply; give the installation's name again.

```bash
scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster --reset-values --installation-name nereus
```

### 4. Verify main before it is published

`scripts/deploy/line` compares the new `main` with the last green commit, else the highest tag, on the paths a release is built from, and runs `make scene-core` on it in a kept worktree. A merge that changed none of those paths is green by inheritance.

```bash
scripts/deploy/line run
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
fetch: origin/main is dde5f73 (last verified none)
paths: changed since v0.1.8: api/ cli/ controllers/ Makefile
scene: make scene-core on dde5f73 in ../nereus-line
ok: scene-core passed in 13m05s
publish: off (would run: make release)
== line green: dde5f73
```

A failed scene marks the line red, keeps its log in `~/.local/state/nereus/line/<commit>.log` and exits non-zero. `run --publish` runs `make release` only after a green scene; a file `.deploy-paused` in the main clone's root suspends every run.

## Check it worked

The smoke test only reads: every Deployment of `nereus-system` rolled out, the annotation equals the commit, the API answers `/healthz`, and [`nereus doctor`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#doctor) passes. Run it alone any time.

```bash
scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster --smoke-only
```

`scripts/deploy/line status` shows the last verified commit and whether the line is paused.

```bash
scripts/deploy/line status
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
main     dde5f73  green  2026-11-15 05:25  scene-core 13m05s
paused   no   (<main clone>/.deploy-paused)
```

## Next

- [Meet the time SLO](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/slo/) for the scenes the line runs.

## Learn more

- `scripts/deploy/live --help`: the settings, all options or environment variables (`NEREUS_CHART_REF`, `NEREUS_CHART_VERSION`, `NEREUS_LIVE_INGRESS_ADDRESS`), so the repository holds no address or token.
- The line is a stand-in: on the platform, k3d-nereus mirrors `main` and builds it (#159, #1613).

# Rebuild the kept cluster

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/kept-cluster.md

Rebuild `k3d-nereus`, the kept cluster used as production, from nothing: the profile `internal-developer-platform` Ready, and Triton, the realm and the portal at their public hostnames.

!!! warning "The owner's job"
    An agent never deletes or recreates this cluster: the guard `.claude/hooks/guard-kept-cluster` refuses it. The rebuild loses OpenBao's secrets, Keycloak's database and the NATS streams of Triton's orders.

## Before you start

- A clone on `main`, and no scene of another session using the registry `localhost:5111`.
- `~/.config/nereus/google-keycloak.env`, exporting `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` of the Google OAuth client.
- The tunnel's credentials, `~/.cloudflared/<UUID>.json` from `cloudflared tunnel create nereus`, mode 0400: the one piece that cannot be made again without Cloudflare's dashboard. On a new machine, copy `~/.cloudflared/` and `~/.config/nereus/`.

## Steps

### 1. Build the CLI and every Nereid from the checkout

`nereus init` installs the images at the version of the `nereus` on the PATH, and `make nereids` tags them with the checkout's version, so build both from the same commit: `make cli`, then `make nereids`.

### 2. Delete and create the cluster

In the owner's terminal (in Claude Code, `!` first): `k3d cluster delete nereus`, then [`nereus init`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#init-profile), which sets the [time zone](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/usage/#3-cut-the-days-where-you-live). About 9 minutes; the tenancy tree comes with it.

```bash
nereus init \
  --target k3d \
  --create-cluster \
  --name nereus \
  --profile internal-developer-platform \
  --yes
```

### 3. Log in as the initial admin

The realm answers at `http://auth.localhost:8080` from the start. [`nereus login --initial-admin`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#login-initial-admin) reads the admin's password with your kubeconfig.

```bash
nereus login --initial-admin
```

### 4. Bring up the tunnel and trust it at the ingress gateway

Apply the edge Reef and its Nereid `cloudflare` ([Publish at a hostname](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/edge/)), keep the credentials file as `edge/cloudflare-tunnel` and an API token (DNS Edit on the zone, Tunnel Read) as `edge/cloudflare-token`, then create the Mandate with `--param tunnel=nereus --param credentialsSecret=edge/cloudflare-tunnel --param apiTokenSecret=edge/cloudflare-token --default`. Create the routes at once.

```bash
nereus edge route create triton --hostname triton.getnereus.dev
```

Repeat for `auth`, `portal` and `api`; the Nereid makes each CNAME. The chart's API route answers only at `localhost`; this one adds `portal` and `api`:

```bash
kubectl apply --filename deploy/ingress/nereus-api-public.yaml
```

Give the Installation its public address (#2291):

```bash
nereus config installation set --public-url https://api.getnereus.dev
```

The CLI and the MCP then use `api.` (#2248).

`numTrustedProxies: 1` keeps cloudflared's `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, so Keycloak's issuer stays `https://`. Write the Release `istio-gateway` with `--values-file deploy/ingress/istio-gateway-values.yaml --dry-run --output yaml`, [`nereus release apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#release-apply) it, then `kubectl apply --filename deploy/ingress/gateway.yaml`.

### 5. Put Google in the realm

Only once the tunnel answers. Source the env file, keep the pair as the secret `google-oauth-keycloak`, then apply the Mandate; `mandate apply` replaces every param, so all go together. Then `nereus logout` and `nereus login` at the public realm.

```bash
nereus mandate apply keycloak \
  --reef authentication \
  --nereid keycloak \
  --param publicUrl=https://auth.getnereus.dev \
  --param googleSecret=google-oauth-keycloak \
  --param googleUsers=owner@example.com \
  --param googleAdmins=owner@example.com \
  --param googleTeam=teammate@example.com
```

`googleTeam` is Triton's team; each person then runs `nereus login https://api.getnereus.dev`.

### 6. Set the portal's address and bring up Triton

[`nereus mandate apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#mandate-apply) `nereus-portal` with `--param publicUrl=https://portal.getnereus.dev`.

Then the Mandate `messaging-nats` is the messaging Reef's default with no match (`--default`, no `--match`), so it holds the Rooms' Topics, which name no engine (ADR 0030).

A cluster that had `--param agents=true` there keeps the old streams of the account `AGENTS` on the claim, unread, and the Secret `nats-triton` of `nereus-system`: drop the parameter, run `nereus nereid apply nats --reef messaging` again, and delete the Secret by hand.

The rooms Reef needs no parameter and no NATS account of its own (#2078). Triton's issuer is the public realm of step 5, given with `--set` (#2157); without it Triton stops with `--issuer is required`.

```bash
nereus reef apply rooms
nereus nereid apply triton \
  --reef rooms \
  --set TRITON_ISSUER=https://auth.getnereus.dev/realms/nereus \
  --set TRITON_JWKS_URL=http://keycloak-server-http.nereus-system.svc:8180/realms/nereus/protocol/openid-connect/certs \
  --set TRITON_RESOURCE_URL=https://triton.getnereus.dev/mcp
```

`POST https://triton.getnereus.dev/mcp` with no token answers 401.

Every other login is gone with the old realm: the claude.ai connector `Triton` signs in again, and a token saved from the old realm no longer works.

### 7. Make yourself an administrator User

A new instance has no User or binding, so your every call passes through the `nereus-admins` emergency exit (ADR 0027, teams, roles and Users) and `nereus doctor` warns `emergency-exit`. [`nereus user create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#user-create) takes the e-mail of step 5; [`nereus authorization binding create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#binding-create) gives it `administrator` (#2159).

```bash
nereus user create owner --email owner@example.com
nereus authorization binding create owner-admin --role administrator --user owner
nereus authorization can-i create core/users
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/users/owner created
✓ authorization/bindings/owner-admin created
yes: authorization/bindings/owner-admin gives administrator to user/owner at the whole instance
```

From then on your calls take the normal check, and the doctor's count of emergency-exit passes stops growing; its warning goes when the API restarts. You stay in `nereus-admins`, so the exit is still there for an emergency.

## Check it worked

[`nereus status`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#status) shows every Reef Ready; `curl` on `https://triton.getnereus.dev/healthz`, `https://portal.getnereus.dev/` and `https://api.getnereus.dev/.well-known/nereus-configuration` answers 200, and the realm `master` answers 404 from outside.

```bash
nereus status
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
REEF            NEREID           VERSION  STATUS  AGE
authentication  keycloak         0.1.0    Ready   7m
catalog         catalog          0.1.0    Ready   1m
core            nereus-api       0.1.0    Ready   9m
                thetis           0.1.0    Ready   9m
database        cloudnative-pg   0.1.0    Ready   7m
delivery        kubernetes       0.1.0    Ready   1m
environment     vcluster         0.1.0    Ready   1m
metrics         victoriametrics  0.1.0    Ready   3m
portal          nereus-portal    0.1.0    Ready   3m
registry        zot              0.1.0    Ready   1m
release         flux             0.1.0    Ready   7m
secrets         openbao          0.1.0    Ready   9m
tenancy         -                -        Ready   9m
Registry  localhost:5111
```

## Next

- [Update the kept cluster without a rebuild](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/kept-cluster-update/): one Nereid, or the API.
- [Deploy main to the live cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/deploy-live/).

# Update the kept cluster without a rebuild

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/kept-cluster-update.md

Move one Nereid, or the Nereus API and its charts, of the kept cluster `k3d-nereus` to a new build, keeping the Installation and every Reef, Nereid and secret.

## Before you start

- The kept cluster of [Rebuild the kept cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/kept-cluster/), and a clone on `main`.
- No scene of another session using the registry `localhost:5111`.

## Steps

### 1. Build one Nereid's image

Build it from `main` under the tag the cluster runs, then push it: `make nereid-sdk`, then `docker build --build-arg API_GROUP=core.getnereus.dev --build-context nereid-sdk=lib/nereid/dist --tag localhost:5111/keycloak-controller:0.1.0 controllers/keycloak`, then `docker push` that tag. `make nereids NEREIDS=keycloak` builds the same image but also rebuilds the API and thetis.

### 2. See what changes

[`nereus nereid apply --image`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-apply-image) with `--dry-run` compares the digest the Deployment pins with the new one.

```bash
nereus nereid apply keycloak \
  --image localhost:5111/keycloak-controller:0.1.0 \
  --dry-run
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Would configure core/nereids/keycloak for reef authentication: image sha256:7daa642492a8 → sha256:3a50a7f56b45.
Nothing changed (--dry-run).
```

### 3. Apply it in place

The Deployment pins the new digest, and the Nereid's next pass applies what changed. Triton is a Nereid too, so it moves the same way.

```bash
nereus nereid apply keycloak \
  --image localhost:5111/keycloak-controller:0.1.0
```

### 4. Move the API and the charts

Run `make cli`, then `make nereids`, so the CLI and the images share a version. [`nereus init`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#init) without `--create-cluster` upgrades the charts `nereus-reefs` and `nereus` in place; the API is ready a few seconds after the `nereus` line.

When the registry lacks an image at the CLI's version (`make cli` ran again after `make nereids`), init stops at its `images` step, before the `nereus` line, and changes nothing:

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ images                    0.0s
  total                     0.0s  slo 8m, 0% green
✗ 2 images the release names are not in their registry: nereus-api, thetis
  nereus-api  localhost:5111/nereus-api:0.1.41.dev146
  thetis      localhost:5111/thetis-controller:0.1.41.dev146
  fix         make nereids
```

Run the `fix` line, then init again. A Pod that cannot pull its image anyway (`ImagePullBackOff`) stops the `ready` step at once, naming the Pod, its image and the same `fix`, instead of waiting for the step's timeout of 30 minutes.

```bash
nereus init \
  --target k3d \
  --name nereus \
  --profile internal-developer-platform \
  --yes
```

The output below is what `test/scene-core-upgrade` prints on its cluster, profile `reference`, after one Nereid was applied by hand: only that one stops, and the other six already run their new digests.

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ kinds          1.2s  release nereus-reefs revision 2
✓ nereus         3.3s  release nereus revision 2, profile reference, images localhost:5111 at 0.1.41.dev129-nereus-scn-2031-9bab4b-next
✓ installation   0.3s  kept nereus-scn-2031-9bab4b
✗ ready         1m32s
  total         1m37s  slo 8m, 20% green
✗ the cluster's Nereids keep their images: thetis does not change an image that is already there
  reference-secrets  localhost:5111/reference-secrets-controller@sha256:0de294bd2444 → @sha256:780a0ec273e5
  fix                nereus nereid apply reference-secrets --reef secrets --image localhost:5111/reference-secrets-controller@sha256:780a0ec273e5ca09d10175bb3835eb75e899fbc34f2718c5a795bd8e79b71a93
```

thetis moves in place every Nereid whose image it installed itself: it records that image on the Nereid (the annotation `core.getnereus.dev/profile-image`), and while the Nereid still runs it, the new one replaces it. When nothing stops it, init's `ready` line counts them (`7 Nereids ready, 6 moved by thetis`).

A Nereid whose image was applied by hand, as in step 3, keeps it: thetis marks its step `Blocked`, reason `ImageApplied`, and the Profile's Ready condition says `ImageApplied`.

init stops as soon as it reads that, instead of waiting for its timeout, and names only those Nereids; the API, the charts and the Nereids it moved stay as they are. [`nereus doctor`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#doctor) shows the same list in its `profile` row.

A Profile that names an image its registry lacks moves nothing either. thetis reads each image before it applies a Nereid: the step is `Blocked`, reason `ImageMissing`, with the image, and the steps after it go on, so a Nereid already there keeps its own. The Profile's Ready condition says `ImageMissing`; init stops at once and adds the fix:

```text
✗ ready          2 Nereids name an image the registry lacks: database, secrets
  database  localhost:5111/database-controller:0.1.41.dev146
  secrets   localhost:5111/secrets-controller:0.1.41.dev146
  fix       make nereids
```

`nereus doctor`'s `profile` row says the same, with the same fix, before any image a Nereid keeps.

A registry that does not answer leaves the step `Waiting` for the next pass.

A Nereid installed before thetis recorded its images has no annotation, so the first update after it lists every such Nereid once; their `fix` lines adopt them, and the next update moves them.

### 5. Move each Nereid applied by hand that should change

Run each `fix` line init printed, as in steps 2 and 3. thetis's next pass finds every image as the Profile names it, records it, and the Profile turns Ready.

## Check it worked

[`nereus nereid list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-list) shows each Nereid Ready with the image you applied, and [`nereus status`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#status) shows every Reef Ready.

## Next

- [Rebuild the kept cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/kept-cluster/) when an in-place update is not enough.
- [Get a Reef's commands working again](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/troubleshoot/nereid-stops/) when a Nereid has no pod serving.

# Meet the time SLO

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/slo.md

See and change the time objective `nereus init` is measured against: 8 minutes on k3d, 20 on a cloud, by default ([spec 0004](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0004-init-time-slo/)).

## Before you start

- A cluster from [Prepare the cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/). The defaults live in the CLI; the cluster may override them in one `ServiceLevelObjective` object in `nereus-system`, whose name and shape are provisional.

## Steps

### 1. See each value and where it came from

[`nereus config slo show`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#slo-show) prints the objective of each target (`local`, `cloud`), the shares of it where the clock changes colour (`yellow`, `orange`, `red`), and the `tolerance`. `cloud` is recorded, not checked yet.

```bash
nereus config slo show
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
SETTING    VALUE  SOURCE
local      8m     default
cloud      20m    default
yellow     50%    default
orange     75%    default
red        100%   default
tolerance  20%    default
```

### 2. Change some

[`nereus config slo set`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#slo-set) writes only what you give; the rest keep their defaults.

```bash
nereus config slo set --local 4m --tolerance 5
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
SETTING    VALUE  SOURCE
local      4m     cluster
cloud      20m    default
yellow     50%    default
orange     75%    default
red        100%   default
tolerance  5%     cluster
```

### 3. Read the bands on the next init

The next [`nereus init`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#init) reads them once its kinds are applied: on a cluster it just created, the defaults hold. A step that crossed into a band says so on its line; red reports a miss, and `init` still finishes. With a tight objective (`--local 1s --yellow 10 --orange 20 --red 30`), its last lines read:

```bash
nereus init --yes
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ prerequisites             0.0s  docker 29.9.1, k3d 5.9.0, helm 4.1.4
✓ registry localhost:5111   0.0s  reused
✓ cluster nereus-local      0.1s  reused
✓ kinds                     0.4s  release nereus-reefs revision 2  slo 47% red
✓ nereus                    1.1s  release nereus revision 2, profile core
✓ installation              0.3s  kept nereus-local
  total                     1.8s  slo 1s, 180% red
```

Past the objective, `init` warns with the slowest steps and the command that raises it. With `--check-slo`, which the scenes that install a profile pass, `init` fails past objective plus tolerance and names the three slowest steps.

## Check it worked

`nereus config slo show` prints `cluster` as the source of each value you set. A cluster set up before #313 may hold the former key `spec.targets.azure`: the table then opens with a warning, and any `nereus config slo set` moves it to `cloud`.

## Clean up

[`nereus config slo reset`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#slo-reset) deletes the object, and every value is back to its default.

```bash
nereus config slo reset
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ SLO reset: every value is back to its default
```

## Next

- [Rebuild the kept cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/kept-cluster/), whose `init` the objective measures.

# Prepare the undercloud

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/undercloud.md

Create the installation's undercloud, `<installation>-undercloud`, a local cluster with the `cloud` Reef whose public OIDC issuer a cloud trusts, here Azure.

!!! note "Recorded against fakes"
    The outputs are what `init` prints in its tests, against a fake k3d, a fake Nereid, a fake `az` and recorded Azure answers. A real subscription is checked by hand (#266).

## Before you start

- What [Prepare the cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/) needs, plus the image of the Nereid `azure` in the local registry: `init` reads its login label before the cluster exists, and stops naming it when it is missing.
- `az login` done, with rights to create a resource group, a storage account and a managed identity.

## Steps

### 1. Name the cloud and the installation

The settings file names both; a cloud target needs the installation's name, since it names everything created in the cloud. `--target azure --installation-name tailwind` does the same without a file.

```yaml
apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: InitConfig
spec:
  cloud: azure
---
apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Installation
metadata:
  name: tailwind
spec:
  id: 0b7e4c1a-93d2-4f6e-8a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b
  alias: tailwind
```

### 2. See the plan

[`nereus init --dry-run`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#init-target) computes the issuer's URL from the installation's id, creates the cluster with it, and prints the plan for Azure; nothing runs there. `--show-requests` adds why each resource exists, each request's URL and its tags.

```bash
nereus init --dry-run --yes
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ undercloud tailwind-undercloud on k3d    0s
✓ installation tailwind, new               0s
✓ Reef cloud, Nereid azure    0s

Plan for Azure · northeurope · 9 requests · not run (--dry-run)
  1  create   resource group        tailwind-platform
  2  create   storage account       issuers0b7e4c1a93d24f6e
  3  create   container             oidc
  4  access   Storage Blob Data Contributor on issuers0b7e4c1a93d24f6e to you
  5  publish  issuer documents (3)
  6  create   managed identity      tailwind-cloud-provisioner
  7  create   federated credential  tailwind-undercloud-azure
  tagged with the installation and who asked
  --show-requests for the why, URLs and tags

Nothing ran in Azure. To run it:
$ nereus init --yes --approve-access
```

### 3. Approve and run it

Without `--approve-access`, `init` asks `Approve 9 requests? [y/N]`, and a non-interactive run stops. Each line then shows its progress, ending with the proof that Azure trusts the undercloud: the Nereid `azure` exchanging its token.

```bash
nereus init --yes --approve-access
```

A request Azure refuses marks its line `✗` and says what an administrator has to run ([Connect to the cloud](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/cloud/)).

### 4. Run it again

The cluster, the installation and the Reef are kept, and the plan is made again. When the published keys are the cluster's own, nothing is uploaded; when they changed, the issuer is marked `Stale` and the upload planned. A cluster presenting another issuer is recreated, but only one whose namespace says `undercloud` and whose Installation has this name and id.

## Check it worked

The run ends with `✓ azure exchanged its token as tailwind-cloud-provisioner`. Each run that sends requests writes a log, readable by you alone, in `~/.local/state/nereus/logs/`: the plan, each request and its answer's status, never a token.

## Next

- [Connect to the cloud](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/cloud/): the Nereid `azure` and what it may do.
- [Meet the time SLO](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/slo/): the cloud target counts against 20 minutes.

## Learn more

- [Undercloud and overcloud](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/undercloud-overcloud/).
- [Spec 0005](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0005-cloud-reef/): the cloud Reef and the issuer.

# Connect to the cloud

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/cloud.md

Apply the Nereid `azure` of the `cloud` Reef: it plans the cloud requests, and the CLI shows them in plain words, asks, and runs them on your machine with your short-lived token, which never leaves it.

!!! note "Recorded against fakes"
    The outputs are what the CLI prints in its tests, against a fake Nereid, `az` and cloud. A real subscription is checked by hand with `test/scene-azure` (#266).

## Before you start

- A cluster whose issuer Azure can reach: [Prepare the undercloud](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/undercloud/) runs these steps for you; run them by hand on an existing cluster or for another subscription.
- `az login` done, and a default location (`az config set defaults.location=westeurope`) or `--param location=<region>` below.
- The `cloud` Reef applied: `nereus reef apply cloud --from-file ./reefs/cloud/`.

## Steps

### 1. See the plan, run nothing

[`nereus nereid apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-apply) reads your login, writes the Mandate and the `Cloud` Instance `default`, waits for the Nereid's plan and shows it. With `--dry-run`, no cloud request is sent.

```bash
nereus nereid apply azure \
  --reef cloud \
  --dry-run \
  --param location=northeurope
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ image            0.0s  cloud-azure-controller:0.1.0 implements cloud, login az
✓ login            0.0s  az, account 00000000-…, organization from the login
✓ plan             0.0s  3 requests for cloud (r-01m5bk)

Plan for Azure · northeurope · 3 requests · not run (--dry-run)
  1  create  resource group        tailwind-platform
  2  create  managed identity      tailwind-cloud-provisioner
  3  create  federated credential  tailwind-undercloud-azure
  tagged with the installation and who asked
  --show-requests for the why, URLs and tags

Nothing ran in Azure. To run it:
$ nereus nereid apply azure --reef cloud --param location=northeurope --approve-access
```

The CLI derives each line's words from the request's method, URL and body, never from text the Nereid sends, so what you read is what runs. `--show-requests` adds each step's why, method, URL and tags.

### 2. Approve and run it

Without `--approve-access`, the CLI asks `Approve 3 requests? [y/N]`; a non-interactive run prints the plan and stops. Each line then gets `✓` and its time, and the run ends with the proof: the Nereid exchanging its token.

```bash
nereus nereid apply azure \
  --reef cloud \
  --param location=northeurope \
  --approve-access
```

### 3. Pick another subscription or location

`--param account=<subscription id>` uses another subscription of the same login; `--param location=<region>` writes the location, which a later run keeps.

### 4. Use an identity an administrator created

When you may not create identities, `--param identity=<client-id>` names one an administrator created. A first plan checks it is in the account; only once its client id matches does the Nereid plan its federated credential, so another identity is never trusted.

## Check it worked

The run ends with `✓ azure exchanged its token as tailwind-cloud-provisioner`. Every resource carries tags naming the installation, who asked and why it exists; the CLI shows no plan with a resource that lacks them.

## Next

- [The Nereid refused the Instance](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/troubleshoot/issuer-not-public/), when the cluster's issuer is not public.
- [A cloud request is refused](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/troubleshoot/request-refused/), when you lack a right.
- [Grant access](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/grant-access/): what the Reefs ask of the cloud.

## Learn more

- [Spec 0005](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0005-cloud-reef/#the-azure-nereid): the Nereid `azure` and the requester tags.

# Publish at a hostname

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/edge.md

Publish a Reef's endpoint, here Triton, at a hostname of your own domain, while Nereus runs on your machine behind a Cloudflare tunnel.

## Before you start

- A cluster from [Prepare the cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/) with the secrets Reef: the Nereid `cloudflare` requires it, and makes the vault `edge`.
- A domain, a Cloudflare account on the free plan, and a named tunnel's credentials from `cloudflared tunnel create nereus`, in `~/.cloudflared/<UUID>.json`.

## Steps

### 1. Apply the edge Reef

[`nereus reef apply edge`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#apply-reef) adds the kinds `Zone`, `Domain` and `Route`.

```bash
nereus reef apply edge
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/edge 0.1.0 created
```

### 2. Apply the Nereid cloudflare

[`nereus nereid apply cloudflare`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#apply-cloudflare) runs the zone and the tunnel.

```bash
nereus nereid apply cloudflare --reef edge
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/cloudflare created, Ready
```

### 3. Keep the tunnel's credentials and name the tunnel

Keep the credentials file as the secret `edge/cloudflare-tunnel` with `nereus secrets create edge/cloudflare-tunnel --from-file credentials.json=<file>` ([Keep a secret](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/secrets/)). Then the Mandate names the tunnel and that secret.

```bash
nereus mandate create cloudflare \
  --reef edge \
  --nereid cloudflare \
  --param tunnel=nereus \
  --param credentialsSecret=edge/cloudflare-tunnel \
  --default
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/mandates/cloudflare created (reef: edge, nereid: cloudflare, default)
```

### 4. Delegate the domain

[`nereus edge zone create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#zone-create) makes the zone and prints its nameservers; point your registrar at them.

```bash
nereus edge zone create getnereus.dev --mandate cloudflare
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ edge/zones/getnereus.dev created, waiting for its delegation
  nameservers: ada.ns.cloudflare.com, bob.ns.cloudflare.com
  point the registrar of getnereus.dev at them; the zone turns Active once Cloudflare sees it
```

When the domain is registered at GoDaddy, the Nereid godaddy points it there for you (#475): [`nereus nereid apply godaddy`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#apply-godaddy), its Mandate with GoDaddy's key and secret in the vault `edge`, then [`nereus edge domain apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#domain-apply).

```bash
nereus edge domain apply getnereus.dev --nameservers-from zone/getnereus.dev --wait
```

GoDaddy answers 403 to an account that may not use its production Domains API; the Domain then says `RegistrarRefused`, and the registrar is changed by hand.

### 5. Carry the hostname through the tunnel

[`nereus edge route create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#route-hostname) carries a hostname to the ingress gateway. Create the routes right after the Mandate: until one exists, the tunnel answers 404 for every hostname.

```bash
nereus edge route create triton --hostname triton.getnereus.dev
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ edge/routes/triton created, Ready: https://triton.getnereus.dev
```

A route may also name the endpoint a Reef publishes, never a cluster, a namespace, a Service or a port (#1951). [`nereus edge endpoint list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#endpoint-list) shows every endpoint the Nereids publish, with the hostnames each one serves; none is published by default. The Nereid's own apply grants one, then the route names it:

```bash
nereus edge endpoint list
nereus nereid apply triton --reef rooms --publish mcp
nereus edge route create triton --hostname triton.getnereus.dev --endpoint rooms/mcp
```

The tunnel carries the hostname only when the endpoint is publishable, granted and served on that hostname; otherwise the route says why (`NotPublished`, `NotServed`, `NoEndpoint`, or `Exposes` when the hostname also serves an endpoint that may not leave the cluster: the tunnel carries the whole hostname). The kept cluster's routes move to endpoints with #2011.

Only a Nereid with an HTTPRoute of its own on the hostname counts for `Exposes`: what a Nereid says in its status alone never takes another Nereid's route off the air.

Any other HTTPRoute the entrance's Gateway admits on the hostname makes the route `Exposes` too, naming it as `<namespace>/<name>`: one with no Nereid label (the chart's `nereus-api`, one a Release made), one of another namespace, or one whose Nereid publishes no granted endpoint there. Give such a host its own hostname, or publish its endpoint.

## Check it worked

`nereus edge zone list` shows the zone Active once the delegation arrives, and `nereus edge route list` shows every hostname the platform answers; then `https://triton.getnereus.dev` answers.

```bash
nereus edge route list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME     HOSTNAME               ENDPOINT  MANDATE     READY   URL
auth     auth.getnereus.dev     -         cloudflare  True    https://auth.getnereus.dev
portal   portal.getnereus.dev   -         cloudflare  True    https://portal.getnereus.dev
triton   triton.getnereus.dev   -         cloudflare  True    https://triton.getnereus.dev
```

## Next

- [Rebuild the kept cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/kept-cluster/), which publishes Triton, the realm and the portal this way.

## Learn more

- With a Cloudflare API token in a secret of the vault `edge` (`--param apiTokenSecret=edge/cloudflare-token` on the Mandate), the Nereid creates or adopts the tunnel itself, with no `cloudflared tunnel create` ([#1961](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1961), `deploy/edge/README.md`).
- ADR 0005: Nereids publish their endpoints and commands in `status`.

# Turn on authentication

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/authentication.md

Turn on sign-in for an installation: the authentication Reef and its Nereid `keycloak` run the realm `nereus`, and every person logs in with `nereus login`, never with a kubeconfig.

## Before you start

- A cluster from [Prepare the cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/). With `--profile internal-developer-platform` the Reef and the Nereid are already there, and step 1 reports `unchanged`.
- After a plain `nereus init`, Nereids for the secrets and release Reefs, the release one with a default Mandate: Keycloak runs as a Release.
- [Tenancy and access](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/tenancy-and-access/) explains who the initial admin is and what `nereus-admins` can do.

## Steps

### 1. Install the Reef and its Nereid

[`nereus reef apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#reef-apply) adds the Reef; [`nereus nereid apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-apply) runs Keycloak and makes the default Mandate `keycloak`.

```bash
nereus reef apply authentication
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/authentication 0.1.0 created (authentication.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: tokens)

Next steps:

  nereus authentication --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef authentication
```

```bash
nereus nereid apply keycloak \
  --reef authentication
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/keycloak created, Ready, pinned to sha256:e8731e3fb833: see 'nereus authentication --help'
  release/releases/keycloak created by core/nereids/keycloak, Ready (codecentric/keycloakx 7.0.1 in namespace nereus-system)
  core/mandates/keycloak created (reef: authentication, nereid: keycloak, default)
  issuer  http://localhost:8180/realms/nereus (dev mode, kept in the Database keycloak)
  client  claude (public, PKCE S256, redirect https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback)
  user    nereus (password: kubectl --namespace nereus-system get secret keycloak-user --output jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode)

Next steps:

  kubectl --namespace nereus-system port-forward service/keycloak-server-http 8180:8180
```

Until its Release is Ready the Nereid reports `WaitingForRelease`; with no default release Mandate it reports `NoReleaseNereid`. On a cluster with an ingress address the realm is served at `http://auth.localhost:8080` and needs no port-forward.

### 2. Log in as the initial admin

The realm's user `nereus` is the instance's initial admin, in `nereus-admins`. [`nereus login --initial-admin`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#login-initial-admin) reads its generated password with your kubeconfig and copies it to the clipboard, never printed. Paste it on the login page.

```bash
nereus login --initial-admin
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
The initial admin's password is in your clipboard (user nereus). Paste it on the login page.
Opening http://auth.localhost:8080/realms/nereus/protocol/openid-connect/auth?... in the browser.
logged in as nereus (nereus-admins), issuer http://auth.localhost:8080/realms/nereus
```

### 3. Give the realm a public host

[`nereus mandate apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#mandate-apply) replaces every param, so name them all. The API trusts one issuer at a time: after the change every person runs `nereus login` again.

```bash
nereus mandate apply keycloak \
  --reef authentication \
  --nereid keycloak \
  --default \
  --param publicUrl=https://auth.example.com
```

### 4. Log in from another machine

[`nereus login`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#login) with the instance's address asks the instance for its identity provider, so no kubeconfig is needed. The address is kept for the next commands.

```bash
KUBECONFIG=/nonexistent nereus login https://nereus.example.com
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Opening https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/protocol/openid-connect/auth?... in the browser.
instance https://nereus.example.com saved in ~/.config/nereus/config.yaml
logged in as ana-silva (nereus-users), issuer https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus
```

On a machine with no browser, add `--use-device-code` and type the code on another device.

## Check it worked

[`nereus whoami`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#whoami) asks the Nereus API who you are.

```bash
nereus whoami
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
ana-silva (nereus-admins, nereus-users)
```

[`nereus status`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#status) now reads through the API with your token, and lists the Reef:

```bash
nereus status
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
REEF            NEREID      VERSION  STATUS  AGE
authentication  keycloak    0.1.0    Ready   2m
core            nereus-api  0.1.0    Ready   4m
                thetis      0.1.0    Ready   4m
release         flux        0.1.0    Ready   3m
secrets         openbao     0.1.0    Ready   4m
tenancy         -           -        Ready   4m

Registry  localhost:5111
```

## Next

- [Grant access](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/grant-access/) to the people of your team.

## Learn more

- [The authentication Reef](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/authentication/): every command, and the realm's clients.
- [ADR 0006](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0006-authentication-reef/): the OIDC contract the default Mandate publishes.

# Grant access

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/grant-access.md

Grant a Nereid that reaches the cloud the roles it asks for: the Nereid acts as its Reef's identity, `<installation>-<reef>-<role>`, with no secret of its own; it asks, and you approve with your own login.

## Before you start

- An installation [connected to the cloud](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/cloud/): the cloud Reef with its Nereid `azure`.
- A Nereid whose image declares `requires: cloud` ([spec 0005](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0005-cloud-reef/)), here `keyvault` for the secrets Reef.
- A cloud login that can create identities and role assignments. A role it cannot write is printed as the command an administrator runs.

!!! note "Recorded against fakes"
    The outputs below come from the CLI's tests, against a fake cloud Nereid and a fake cloud. `test/scene-azure` runs a real subscription.

## Steps

### 1. Apply the Nereid

[`nereus nereid apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-apply) gives the Nereid a short-lived token for the cloud, writes its Reef's access entry and shows the plan that creates its identity.

```bash
nereus nereid apply keyvault \
  --reef secrets
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ image            0.0s  secrets-keyvault-controller:0.1.0 implements secrets, requires cloud
✓ login            0.0s  az, account 00000000-…
✓ mandate          0.0s  core/mandates/keyvault created (reef: secrets, nereid: keyvault, default)
✓ plan             0.1s  2 requests for secrets (r-01m5bk)
  1  create  managed identity      tailwind-secrets-reader  in westeurope
  2  create  federated credential  tailwind-undercloud-keyvault
  tagged with the installation and who asked
  --show-requests for the why, URLs and tags
  log: ~/.local/state/nereus/logs/20261019T221500Z-install.log
Approve 2 requests? [y/N]: y
✓ requests         0.0s  2 applied
✓ ready            0.0s  keyvault reports Ready
  total            0.1s
✓ keyvault added to secrets · acts as tailwind-secrets-reader
```

Another Nereid of the same Reef later keeps the identity and its grants: the plan only swaps the federated credential.

### 2. See what is asked

`nereus system access list` shows each Reef's access entries and the roles its Nereid asks for but nobody approved yet.

```bash
nereus system access list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
REEF       REQUEST        WHAT                                                                                                              STATE
cloud      r-01jaq3…m2n3  identity tailwind-cloud-provisioner                                                                               Applied
secrets    r-01m59t…zejf  identity tailwind-secrets-reader                                                                                  Applied
secrets    -              grant Key Vault Secrets User on key vault vault-0123456789abcdef in resource group tailwind-platform              Asked
terraform  -              grant Storage Blob Data Contributor on storage account state0123456789abcdef in resource group tailwind-platform  Asked
```

An ask for `Owner`, `User Access Administrator` or `Role Based Access Control Administrator` shows `Refused` and is never copied into a plan.

### 3. Approve

`nereus system access approve --all` turns every Reef's asks into plans, shows them and runs them after one question; `--dry-run` shows them and runs none.

```bash
nereus system access approve --all
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
1/2 secrets  r-01m5bk…5563  2 requests
  1  check   managed identity  tailwind-secrets-reader
  2  access  Key Vault Secrets User on vault-0123456789abcdef to tailwind-secrets-reader
2/2 terraform  r-01m5bk…dh0a  3 requests
  1  create  managed identity      tailwind-terraform-runner  in westeurope
  2  create  federated credential  tailwind-undercloud-stacks
  3  access  Storage Blob Data Contributor on state0123456789abcdef to tailwind-terraform-runner
  tagged with the installation and who asked
  --show-requests for the why, URLs and tags
  log: ~/.local/state/nereus/logs/20261019T221500Z-approve.log
Approve 2 plans (5 requests)? [y/N]: y
✗ 1/2 secrets  r-01m5bk…5563  grant Key Vault Secrets User on vault-0123456789abcdef to tailwind-secrets-reader refused: AuthorizationFailed: The client cannot write role assignments on the account.
    ${0.properties.principalId} = 33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333
An administrator can grant Key Vault Secrets User to tailwind-secrets-reader:
  az role assignment create --assignee-object-id 33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333 --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal --role "Key Vault Secrets User" --scope /subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/tailwind-platform/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/vault-0123456789abcdef
✓ 2/2 terraform  r-01m5bk…dh0a  3 applied
    ${0.properties.principalId} = 33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333
✗ 1 of 2 plans applied: run 'nereus system access approve --all' again to apply what is missing
  log: ~/.local/state/nereus/logs/20261019T221500Z-approve.log
```

A failed plan undoes none of the others. Hand the printed `az` line to an administrator, or approve with a login that holds the right.

## Check it worked

Run the approval again: it plans only what is still missing, and ends with every plan applied.

```bash
nereus system access approve --all
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
1/1 secrets  r-01m5bk…satf  2 requests
  1  check   managed identity  tailwind-secrets-reader
  2  access  Key Vault Secrets User on vault-0123456789abcdef to tailwind-secrets-reader
  --show-requests for the why, URLs and tags
  log: ~/.local/state/nereus/logs/20261019T221500Z-approve.log
Approve 2 requests? [y/N]: y
✓ 1/1 secrets  r-01m5bk…satf  2 applied
    ${0.properties.principalId} = 33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333
✓ 1 plan applied
```

- [Authorize people](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/authorization/): who may run which command in the installation.

## Learn more

- [Undercloud and overcloud](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/undercloud-overcloud/): why the installation's identity lives in the cloud.

# Say who may do what

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/authorization.md

Give a team a role on a node of the tenancy tree: every member gets it by joining and loses it by leaving, and the Nereus API asks the authorization Reef before every read and write.

## Before you start

- A cluster from [Prepare the cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/) with `--profile internal-developer-platform`: it brings the teams Reef, the authorization Reef and its Nereid `openfga` with the default Mandate that turns the check on. Before that Mandate exists, only `nereus-admins` passes.
- A Project to own the team, from [Know whose each thing is](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/tenancy/): `project/payments` below.
- [Tenancy and access](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/tenancy-and-access/) tells a User, a Team, a Role and a Binding apart.

## Steps

### 1. Register the people

[`nereus user create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#user-create) records the e-mail the person's first sign-in is matched with. A login with no User may do nothing.

```bash
nereus user create ana --email ana@example.com
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/users/ana created
```

```bash
nereus user create bruno --email bruno@example.com
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/users/bruno created

Next steps:

  nereus teams create <team> --owner project/<project>
```

### 2. Make the team and name its tech lead

[`nereus teams create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#team-create) makes the team under its Project; [`nereus teams member create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#member-lead) adds a member, here with the position `tech-lead`.

```bash
nereus teams create payments --owner project/payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ teams/teams/payments created

Next steps:

  nereus teams member create <user> --team payments
```

```bash
nereus teams member create ana \
  --team payments \
  --position tech-lead
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ teams/teams/payments/members/ana created

Next steps:

  nereus teams get payments
```

### 3. Give the team a role

[`nereus authorization role list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#role-list) shows the roles: `administrator` is built in and cannot change; `viewer`, `developer` and `team-lead` are examples to edit. [`nereus authorization binding create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#binding-team) makes every member a developer of the Project.

```bash
nereus authorization binding create payments-developers \
  --role developer \
  --team payments \
  --owner project/payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ authorization/bindings/payments-developers created

Next steps:

  nereus authorization binding list --owner project/payments
```

### 4. Give one position a role

With [`--position`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#binding-position), only the team's tech lead gets `team-lead`, which may create Environments.

```bash
nereus authorization binding create payments-leads \
  --role team-lead \
  --team payments \
  --position tech-lead \
  --owner project/payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ authorization/bindings/payments-leads created

Next steps:

  nereus authorization binding list --owner project/payments
```

## Check it worked

[`nereus authorization binding list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#binding-list) shows who holds what on the Project.

```bash
nereus authorization binding list --owner project/payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME                 SUBJECT                         ROLE       OWNER
mobile-leads         team/payments-mobile/tech-lead  team-lead  project/payments
payments-developers  team/payments                   developer  project/payments
payments-leads       team/payments/tech-lead         team-lead  project/payments
```

[`nereus authorization can-i`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#can-i-yes) answers with the binding that allows it. With no `--user` it asks about you.

```bash
nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments \
  --owner project/payments \
  --user ana
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
yes: authorization/bindings/payments-leads gives team-lead to team/payments/tech-lead at project/payments
```

Signed in as Bruno, creating an Environment there is refused, and nothing changes:

```bash
nereus environment create staging --owner project/payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ environment/environments/staging: bruno may not create environment/environments at project/payments. To see who may, run:
  nereus authorization binding list --owner project/payments
  Nothing was changed.
```

## Next

- [Know whose each thing is](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/tenancy/): the tree a binding reaches down.

## Learn more

- [The authorization Reef](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/authorization/) and [the teams Reef](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/teams/): every command, presenting rights included.
- [ADR 0027](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0027-teams-roles-and-users/): users, teams, roles and bindings.

# Know whose each thing is

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/tenancy.md

Build the installation's tenancy tree, Organizations with Projects under them, so every Workload, Environment and database names who it belongs to.

## Before you start

- A cluster from [Prepare the cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/), in any profile: `nereus init` installs the tenancy Reef, its admission policy and the tree in `tenancy/`. The Reef has no Nereid.
- [Tenancy and access](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/tenancy-and-access/) explains the tree and what an `owner` points at.

## Steps

### 1. Create an Organization

[`nereus tenancy organization create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#organization-create) makes the top of a tree, its boundary.

```bash
nereus tenancy organization create example
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ tenancy/organizations/example created

Next steps:

  nereus tenancy organization list
```

### 2. Add a Project under it

[`nereus tenancy project create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#project-create) needs a parent that exists; the line shows the full path. `--dry-run --output yaml` prints the object as `apply` takes it.

```bash
nereus tenancy project create shop \
  --parent organization/example \
  --repository https://github.com/example/shop
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ tenancy/organizations/example/projects/shop created

Next steps:

  nereus tenancy project list
```

### 3. Nest a Project

A Project can sit under another [Project](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#project-nested). A parent that does not exist is refused, and nothing is written.

```bash
nereus tenancy project create checkout --parent project/shop
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ tenancy/organizations/example/projects/shop/projects/checkout created

Next steps:

  nereus tenancy project list
```

### 4. Make a Project your default owner

[`nereus config set owner`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#config-owner) names the owner the next commands use when you give none.

```bash
nereus config set owner project/checkout
```

The kinds come from the installation, not the CLI: an installation whose `reefs/tenancy/` adds `Department` and `Squad` gets `nereus tenancy squad create` the same way. To keep the tree in files, [`nereus tenancy apply --from-file tenancy/`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#apply) writes parents before children.

## Check it worked

[`nereus tenancy project get`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#project-get) shows the full path and the boundary Organization.

```bash
nereus tenancy project get checkout
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:        checkout
Kind:        Project
Path:        tenancy/organizations/example/projects/shop/projects/checkout
Parent:      Project/shop
Boundary:    Organization/example
Repository:  -
```

## Clean up

!!! warning "Deletes everything under it"
    `--cascade` deletes every node under the Project, deepest first. Preview it with `--dry-run`.

```bash
nereus tenancy project delete shop --cascade
```

## Next

- [Authorize a team](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/authorization/) on a Project of the tree.

## Learn more

- [The tenancy Reef](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/tenancy/): every command.
- [ADR 0015](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0015-tenancy/): one tree of a fixed shape, with kinds from each installation.

# Prove a GitHub App is installed

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/github-app.md

Connect a GitHub App as a Mandate of the authentication Reef's Nereid `github`: its status proves where the App is installed and what it may do, and consumers ask it for one-hour tokens, never for its key.

## Before you start

- A cluster with the secrets Reef and its vault `default`, from [Keep a secret](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/secrets/).
- An App you already have: its id, and its private key (a `.pem` file). With no App yet, [`nereus authentication app-register`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#app-register) creates one in the browser, and only the Nereid ever holds its key; skip to step 4.
- [Reef, Nereid and Mandate](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/model/): the App is a Mandate, its id and key its params.

## Steps

### 1. Keep the App's private key as a secret

[`nereus secrets create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#create) encrypts it on your machine before it leaves it.

```bash
GITHUB_APP_KEY="$(cat app.pem)" nereus secrets create github-app-key --from-env GITHUB_APP_KEY
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/github-app-key created (key SHA256:l0jt+UOKUmA72jydN0DSpTzFJIdO6wP/xUvdAKryBe4)
Stored encrypted; a Kubernetes Secret is made only when a binding asks for it (#532).
```

### 2. Apply the Nereid

The Nereid is opt-in, outside every profile. [`nereus nereid apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-apply) gives it one namespace, `nereus-system-github`, the only one where it reads Secrets.

```bash
nereus nereid apply github --reef authentication
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/github created, Ready, pinned to sha256:021dd70640d0: see 'nereus authentication --help'
  namespaces/nereus-system-github applied (the github Nereid's Role there, where vault default delivers the App keys)

Next steps:

  nereus mandate create github --reef authentication --nereid github --param appId=<id> --param privateKey=<secret> --param allow=<namespace>:<repository>:<permission>=<level> --default
```

### 3. Create the App's Mandate

[`nereus mandate create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#mandate-create) names the App, its key's secret and who may ask a token. Each `allow` is `<namespace>:<repository or *>:<permission>=<level>`; with none, no token is ever made.

```bash
nereus mandate create github \
  --reef authentication \
  --nereid github \
  --param appId=123456 \
  --param privateKey=github-app-key \
  --param allow=nereus-system:*:contents=read \
  --param allow=example:example/app:metadata=read \
  --default
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/mandates/github created (reef: authentication, nereid: github, default)
  clusterrole/controller-github configured (nereid github writes the status of mandate github)
```

### 4. Lend a repository for an hour

[`nereus authentication token create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#token-create) asks the Mandate for a token of one repository. The Nereid writes it to the Secret `token-<name>` of the Token's namespace; no command prints it.

```bash
nereus authentication token create catalog \
  --repository example/app \
  --permission contents=read
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ authentication/tokens/catalog created (expires in 1h, mandate github)

Next steps:

  nereus authentication token get catalog
```

A namespace the Mandate does not allow gets no token, and the line names the `allow` to add.

## Check it worked

[`nereus mandate get`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#mandate-get) shows the App as GitHub answered, and the allowlist as the Nereid read it.

```bash
nereus mandate get github
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:           github
Reef:           authentication
Nereid:         github
Default:        true
Params:         allow=nereus-system:*:contents=read;example:example/app:metadata=read, appId=123456, privateKey=github-app-key
Status:         Ready
App:            example-nereus
Installations:  example (all repositories)
Permissions:    contents=read, metadata=read
Age:            10s
Allowed:
  NAMESPACE      REPOSITORY   PERMISSIONS
  nereus-system  *            contents=read
  example        example/app  metadata=read
```

Another status names what is wrong: `NotInstalled` with the URL to install the App, `InvalidCredentials` for a key of no App, `MissingParam` for a secret that does not exist.

## Clean up

```bash
nereus authentication token delete catalog
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ authentication/tokens/catalog deleted

Next steps:

  nereus authentication token list
```

## Next

- [Connect a repository host](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/scm-connection/) that builds and mirrors through the App.

## Learn more

- [The authentication Reef](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/authentication/): `app-register`, tokens and every command.
- [ADR 0006](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0006-authentication-reef/): the platform's identity towards an outside system is a Mandate.

# Keep a secret

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/secrets.md

Keep a secret in a vault of the installation: each value is encrypted on your machine before it leaves it, and no command prints it back.

## Before you start

- A cluster from [Prepare the cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/) with `--profile internal-developer-platform`: it brings the secrets Reef, the Nereid `openbao` and the vault `default`.
- The values in environment variables or files, never on the command line, where the shell history keeps them.

## Steps

### 1. Create a secret from environment variables

[`nereus secrets create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#create) encrypts each value with the key of the vault's Mandate, then stores it.

```bash
nereus secrets create google-oauth \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth created (key SHA256:GQ8TrJ9h6ZrNYHItBycWK+tXkURjowfJWcjEyabRIKI)
Stored encrypted; a Kubernetes Secret is made only when a binding asks for it (#532).
```

### 2. Take a key from a file

`--from-file KEY=PATH` takes the file's bytes, for a private key or a certificate.

```bash
nereus secrets create github-app \
  --from-file private-key=key.pem \
  --from-env APP_ID
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/github-app created (key SHA256:GQ8TrJ9h6ZrNYHItBycWK+tXkURjowfJWcjEyabRIKI)
Stored encrypted; a Kubernetes Secret is made only when a binding asks for it (#532).
```

### 3. Change it from a file

`create` refuses a secret that exists. Write the encrypted secret to a file, safe to keep, then [`nereus secrets apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#apply) it; each change is a new version.

```bash
nereus secrets create google-oauth \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET \
  --dry-run --output yaml > google-oauth.yaml
nereus secrets apply --from-file google-oauth.yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth configured
```

## Check it worked

[`nereus secrets list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#list) shows the keys' names, never a value.

```bash
nereus secrets list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
VAULT    NAME          KEYS                  STATUS  AGE
default  github-app    APP_ID, +1            Ready   9s
default  google-oauth  GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, +1  Ready   10s
```

## Clean up

!!! warning "Deleted for good"
    Deleting a secret destroys every version of it in OpenBao.

```bash
nereus secrets delete default/google-oauth
nereus secrets delete github-app
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth deleted
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/github-app deleted
```

## Next

- [Use a secret in a namespace](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/secret-binding/): a binding makes the Kubernetes Secret an app reads.
- [Release a chart](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/release/) that reads a secret through a binding.

## Learn more

- [The secrets Reef](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/secrets/): vaults, secrets and bindings, every command.
- [ADR 0013](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0013-command-conventions/): `create` builds from flags, `apply` takes files.

# Use a secret in a namespace

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/secret-binding.md

Give a namespace a Kubernetes Secret made from a secret of the installation, under the key names its app expects: a binding asks for it, and the vault says which namespaces may.

## Before you start

- A secret `google-oauth` in the vault `default`, from [Keep a secret](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/secrets/).
- The namespace `identity`, such as from `kubectl create namespace identity`.

## Steps

### 1. Allow the namespace

A vault lists the namespaces that may bind its secrets in `spec.allowedNamespaces`. Write the vault as a file with [`nereus secrets vault get`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#binding-refused), add `identity` there, then apply the file.

```bash
nereus secrets vault get default \
  --output yaml > default.yaml
```

```bash
nereus secrets vault apply \
  --from-file default.yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default configured
```

### 2. Bind the secret
