- A cluster from [Prepare the cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/), and `kubectl` for the last two steps.

## Steps

### 1. See which Reef has a problem

[`nereus status`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#status) gives one row per Reef and its Nereid:

```bash
nereus status
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
REEF            NEREID      VERSION  STATUS  AGE
authentication  keycloak    0.1.0    Ready   2m
core            nereus-api  0.1.0    Ready   4m
                thetis      0.1.0    Ready   4m
release         flux        0.1.0    Ready   3m
secrets         openbao     0.1.0    Ready   4m
tenancy         -           -        Ready   4m

Registry  localhost:5111
```

### 2. Look at the Nereid

[`nereus nereid get`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-get) shows its image, digest and Mandates; a Nereid that is not `Ready` also says why (`Unavailable`, `NotConformant`).

```bash
nereus nereid get keycloak
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:         keycloak
Reefs:        authentication
Image:        localhost:5111/keycloak-controller:0.1.0
Digest:       sha256:0f4675ab231b4e6d4a439d0c7d8e5b07011f35802b38592851542cf56666be93
Title:        authentication-keycloak-controller
Description:  The keycloak Nereid of Nereus, for the authentication reef
Status:       Ready
Mandates:     keycloak (default)
Age:          2m
```

### 3. Read the object's events

Each object's `Ready` condition says why in its `message`, and every change of a step is a Kubernetes Event on the object, kept when the Nereid restarts: `kubectl describe` shows them, under Events.

### 4. Read the Nereid's log

A Nereid logs JSON Lines, one per reconcile pass and its reason: `kubectl logs deployment/keycloak --namespace nereus-system`.

## Check it worked

[`nereus doctor`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#doctor) runs ten checks of the installation, pass or fail, and says the next step for one that fails:

```bash
nereus doctor
```

## Next

- [When the Nereid stops](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/troubleshoot/nereid-stops/): `Unavailable`, and how the commands come back.
- [Pass the conformance tests](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/build/conformance/): the status every object must carry.

## Learn more

- [Spec 0003](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0003-nereid-conformance/): the `Ready` condition, the steps and their events.

# The issuer is not public

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/troubleshoot/issuer-not-public.md

`nereus nereid apply azure` stops at the plan, before any cloud request.

## You see

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ image            0.0s  cloud-azure-controller:0.1.0 implements cloud, login az
✓ login            0.0s  az, account 00000000-…, organization from the login
✗ plan             0.0s  the Nereid refused the Instance: IssuerNotPublic
  what     the undercloud of installation tailwind presents Kubernetes' default issuer https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local, which Azure cannot reach
  cause    probably created by nereus init without --target azure (k3d is the default): the issuer is set when the cluster is created and never changes after
  check    kubectl get --raw /.well-known/openid-configuration
  fix      nereus init --target azure --installation-name tailwind
  Nothing ran in the cloud.
```

## Why

The cluster presents Kubernetes' default issuer, which Azure cannot reach. The issuer is set when the cluster is created and never changes after.

## Fix

Create the undercloud with a public issuer, as in [Prepare the undercloud](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/undercloud/):

```bash
nereus init --target azure --installation-name tailwind
```

## Check

`kubectl get --raw /.well-known/openid-configuration` shows an issuer under `blob.core.windows.net`, and the next `nereus nereid apply azure` prints its plan.

# A cloud request is refused

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/troubleshoot/request-refused.md

An approved plan of `nereus nereid apply azure` stops at the first request the cloud refuses.

## You see

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ 1  create  resource group        tailwind-platform              0s
✗ 2  create  managed identity      tailwind-cloud-provisioner     0s
  3  create  federated credential  tailwind-undercloud-azure
  tagged with the installation and who asked
  --show-requests for the why, URLs and tags

✗ create managed identity tailwind-cloud-provisioner refused: AuthorizationFailed: The client cannot create managed identities in tailwind-platform.
  ran: create resource group tailwind-platform
  not run: create managed identity tailwind-cloud-provisioner, create federated credential tailwind-undercloud-azure
An administrator can create the identity, and give you Managed Identity Contributor on it:
  az identity create --resource-group tailwind-platform --name tailwind-cloud-provisioner
  az role assignment create --assignee <your-object-id> --role "Managed Identity Contributor" --scope <identity-id>
Then run:
  nereus nereid apply azure --reef cloud --param identity=<client-id>
  log: ~/.local/state/nereus/logs/20261019T221500Z-install.log
```

## Why

Your login lacks the right to create that resource (`403`). The later requests did not run.

## Fix

Ask an administrator to run the two `az` lines printed, then name the identity they created:

```bash
nereus nereid apply azure --reef cloud --param identity=<client-id>
```

## Check

The run ends with `✓ azure exchanged its token as tailwind-cloud-provisioner`. The log named in the output holds each request and its answer's status.

# authentication

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/authentication.md

Who the person is, and who the platform is towards the systems it acts on.

## Commands

- [`nereus login`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#login) The browser opens, and the login comes back to the terminal
- [`nereus login`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#login-device) A machine with no browser logs in from another device
- [`nereus login`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#login-initial-admin) A new instance has one obvious way in: its initial admin
- [`nereus login`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#login-refresh) A new token without the browser, with the groups read again
- [`nereus logout`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#logout) Logging out ends the session at the identity provider too
- [`nereus whoami`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#whoami) The Nereus API says who you are
- [`nereus authentication app-register`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#app-register) With no App yet, the Nereid creates it in the browser
- [`nereus authentication token create catalog`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#token-create) A Token lends one repository for an hour
- [`nereus authentication token list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authentication.html#token-list) list shows each Token, never its value

## Examples

### login

Authorization code with PKCE, on a listener of 127.0.0.1.

```bash
nereus login
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Opening https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/protocol/openid-connect/auth?... in the browser.
logged in as ana-silva (nereus-users), issuer https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus

Next steps:

  nereus whoami
  https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/account/account-security/signing-in   (set a password, optional)
```

### login-device

The device grant: open the page elsewhere and type the code.

```bash
nereus login \
  --use-device-code
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Open https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/device and enter ABCD-EFGH (expires in 10 minutes).
logged in as ana-silva (nereus-users), issuer https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus

Next steps:

  nereus whoami
  https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/account/account-security/signing-in   (set a password, optional)
```

### login-initial-admin

The password goes to the clipboard, never to the terminal.

```bash
nereus login \
  --initial-admin
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
The initial admin's password is in your clipboard (user nereus). Paste it on the login page.
Opening https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/protocol/openid-connect/auth?... in the browser.
logged in as nereus (nereus-admins), issuer https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus

Next steps:

  nereus whoami
  https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/account/account-security/signing-in   (set a password, optional)
```

### login-refresh

Renew the session, so a group joined since the last login shows.

```bash
nereus login \
  --refresh
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
token refreshed for ana-silva, valid until 14:05
```

### logout

Revoke the session, then delete the credentials.

```bash
nereus logout
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
logged out nereus@example.com: session revoked, ~/.config/nereus/credentials deleted
```

### whoami

GET /v1/me with the token of nereus login.

```bash
nereus whoami
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
ana-silva (nereus-admins, nereus-users)
```

### app-register

An action the github Nereid publishes under the Reef.

```bash
nereus authentication app-register \
  --mandate team \
  --org example-team
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
→ opening the browser to create the GitHub App "nereus-prod"
✓ secrets/team-app-key stored by the Nereid (the key never reaches this machine)
✓ secrets/team-webhook-secret and secrets/team-oauth-client stored by the Nereid
✓ core/mandates/team configured (appId 900001, privateKey team-app-key, webhookSecret team-webhook-secret)

Next steps:

  Install it on the org: https://github.com/apps/nereus-prod/installations/new
  nereus mandate get team
```

### token-create

A token to read one repository, from the default Mandate.

```bash
nereus authentication token create catalog \
  --repository example/app \
  --permission contents=read
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ authentication/tokens/catalog created (expires in 1h, mandate github)

Next steps:

  nereus authentication token get catalog
```

### token-list

Every Token.

```bash
nereus authentication token list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
TOKEN    REPOSITORY   PERMISSIONS    MANDATE  EXPIRES  STATUS
catalog  example/app  contents=read  github   1h       Ready
```

# authorization

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/authorization.md

Every command of the first slice: Users, teams, roles and bindings, and who may do what.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply authorization`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#reef-apply) The authorization Reef brings roles and bindings
- [`nereus profile apply internal-developer-platform`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#nereid-apply) openfga answers who may do what
- [`nereus user create ana`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#user-create) A person is one User, whatever the login
- [`nereus user list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#user-list) Every User, and how many identities each has
- [`nereus authorization role list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#role-list) One built-in role, four examples to edit
- [`nereus authorization role get team-lead`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#role-get) A role is a list of rules: Reef, kinds, verbs
- [`nereus authorization role create release-manager`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#role-create) A new role takes the words the CLI already uses
- [`nereus authorization role delete administrator`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#role-delete) The administrator role cannot be deleted
- [`nereus authorization binding create payments-developers`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#binding-team) A binding gives a role to a team on a node
- [`nereus authorization binding create payments-leads`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#binding-position) A position narrows the binding to the tech lead
- [`nereus authorization binding list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#binding-list) Every binding of a node, and who it reaches
- [`nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#can-i-yes) Ana asks, and the answer names the binding
- [`nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#can-i-no) Bruno may not, and the answer says why
- [`nereus can-i create build/builds`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#can-i-shortcut) The shortcut asks the same question
- [`nereus authorization can-i drive presentations/sessions/platform-day`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#can-i-drive) Presenting is a right: a Session's speakers drive it
- [`nereus authorization can-i assist presentations/sessions/platform-day`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#can-i-assist) The staff assists a Session, and never drives it
- [`nereus environment create staging`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#enforce-denied) Bruno's environment is refused, politely
- [`nereus environment create staging`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#enforce-allowed) Ana's environment is created
- [`nereus teams member delete ana`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#leave-team) [planned #1307] Leaving the team removes the access
- [`nereus environment list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#fail-closed) Without openfga, everything closes
- [`nereus authorization gate create payments-environments`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#gate-create) A Gate says which requests wait, and for whom
- [`nereus environment create staging`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#create-held) [planned #2119] The object exists at once, and stands Pending
- [`nereus authorization approval list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#approval-list) The approver sees what waits for a decision
- [`nereus authorization approval approve staging-create-7f3a`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#approval-approve) Approving lifts the hold, and the Nereid provisions
- [`nereus authorization approval reject staging-create-7f3a`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#approval-reject) Rejecting keeps the history, and provisions nothing
- [`nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/authorization.html#can-i-may-ask) No, but Bruno may ask

## Examples

### reef-apply

The kinds of the Reef.

```bash
nereus reef apply authorization
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/authorization created (authorization.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: bindings, roles)

Next steps:

  nereus nereid apply openfga --reef authorization
```

### nereid-apply

The profile installs the Nereid and its default Mandate (an excerpt).

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ nereid openfga                            1m19s  core/nereids/openfga created, Ready
✓ mandate openfga                            7.0s  core/mandates/openfga created (reef: authorization, nereid: openfga, default)
```

### user-create

The tech lead.

```bash
  --email ana@example.com
```

A role of this instance's own.

### fail-closed

A read while the Nereid does not answer.

```bash

```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
  nereus doctor
  Nothing was changed.
```

### gate-create

Requests to create an Environment in payments wait for an approver.

```bash
nereus authorization gate create payments-environments \
  --reef environment \
  --kinds environments \
  --verbs create \
  --project payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }

Next steps:

  nereus authorization gate list
```

### create-held

A dry run says whose approval it would wait for, and writes nothing.

```bash

  --project payments \
  --dry-run
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
would wait for approval: authorization/gates/payments-environments, approvers team/payments/tech-lead
environment/environments/staging would be created (mandate: vcluster, nereid: vcluster).
Nothing changed (--dry-run).
```

### approval-list

Every held request has one Approval.

```bash
nereus authorization approval list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME                 TARGET                            VERB    REQUESTED BY  PHASE    AGE
staging-create-7f3a  environment/environments/staging  create  bruno         Pending  2m
```

### approval-approve

Ana, of the tech lead team, decides.

```bash
nereus authorization approval approve staging-create-7f3a \
  --reason "sprint demo"
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ authorization/approvals/staging-create-7f3a approved; environment/environments/staging released
```

### approval-reject

Or the approver says no, with the reason.

```bash
nereus authorization approval reject staging-create-7f3a \
  --reason "use the shared staging"
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ authorization/approvals/staging-create-7f3a rejected; environment/environments/staging will not be provisioned
```

### can-i-may-ask

The answer to create is still no, and says who decides.

```bash
nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments \
  --project payments \
  --user bruno
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
no, but may ask: authorization/gates/payments-environments holds create for team/payments/tech-lead's approval
```

# build

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/build.md

Every command that builds an image from a Workload's source inside the cluster.

## Commands

- [`nereus build create hello-1`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/build.html#build-create) create builds a Workload at the commit its Nereid read
- [`nereus build get hello-1`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/build.html#build-get) get shows the digest the registry answered
- [`nereus build list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/build.html#build-list) list shows every build, a line each
- [`nereus build get app-1`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/build.html#build-private) A private repository is fetched with a token for that build alone
- [`nereus build delete hello-1`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/build.html#build-delete) delete removes the Build and its Job, never the image
- [`nereus build trigger create triton`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/build.html#trigger-create) trigger create builds a Workload on each new commit of its Mirror
- [`nereus build trigger list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/build.html#trigger-list) trigger list shows the commit each one saw and its last Build
- [`nereus build trigger get triton`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/build.html#trigger-get) trigger get shows the Mirror it follows and the commit it saw
- [`nereus build trigger delete triton`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/build.html#trigger-delete) trigger delete stops new Builds and leaves the ones it made

## Examples

### build-create

Two Jobs in the namespace builds: fetch, then build and push.

```bash
nereus build create hello-1 \
  --workload hello
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
build/builds/hello-1 created (mandate: buildkit, nereid: buildkit)

Next steps:

  nereus build get hello-1
```

### build-get

Its phase, image and digest.

```bash
nereus build get hello-1
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:          hello-1
Workload:      hello
Commit:        a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012345678
Organization:  -
Project:       -
Mandate:       -
Nereid:        buildkit
Phase:         Succeeded
Image:         localhost:31874/hello:hello-1
Digest:        sha256:3517762d3517762d3517762d3517762d3517762d3517762d3517762d3517762d
Job:           hello-1
```

### build-list

The Workload, the commit, the phase and the digest.

```bash
nereus build list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
BUILD    WORKLOAD  COMMIT   STATUS     DIGEST
hello-1  hello     a1b2c3d  Succeeded  sha256:3517762d3517
hello-2  hello     -        Pending    -
```

### build-private

An allow line for builds on the App's Mandate, then the Build.

```bash
nereus build get app-1
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:      app-1
Workload:  app
Phase:     Running
Message:   source fetched at a1b2c3d from https://github.com/example/app with a token for example/app (contents=read)
```

### build-delete

The image it pushed stays in its Repository.

```bash
nereus build delete hello-1
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
build/builds/hello-1 deleted

Next steps:

  nereus build list
```

### trigger-create

The Mirror nereus copies the source of the Workload triton.

```bash
nereus build trigger create triton \
  --workload triton
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
build/triggers/triton created (mandate: buildkit, nereid: buildkit)

Next steps:

  nereus build trigger get triton
```

### trigger-list

After a push, once the Mirror pulled it.

```bash
nereus build trigger list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
TRIGGER  WORKLOAD  MIRROR  COMMIT   LAST BUILD      STATUS
triton   triton    nereus  a1b2c3d  triton-a1b2c3d  Ready
```

### trigger-get

Its Mirror, branch, commit and last Build.

```bash
nereus build trigger get triton
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:          triton
Workload:      triton
Organization:  getnereus
Project:       nereus/triton
Mandate:       -
Nereid:        buildkit
Mirror:        nereus
Branch:        main
Commit:        a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012345678
Last Build:    triton-a1b2c3d
Status:        Ready
```

### trigger-delete

No new Build of triton; triton-a1b2c3d stays.

```bash
nereus build trigger delete triton
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
build/triggers/triton deleted; the Builds it created stay

Next steps:

  nereus build trigger list
```

# catalog

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/catalog.md

Every command that says what Nereus has: what runs, what is published, and whether it holds together.

## Commands

- [`nereus catalog apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/catalog.html#workload-apply) One apply registers the repository
- [`nereus catalog workload create edge-cloudflare`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/catalog.html#workload-create) create writes an entry from flags
- [`nereus catalog list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/catalog.html#workload-list) list searches by type
- [`nereus catalog delete openbao`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/catalog.html#workload-delete) delete never touches what runs
- [`nereus catalog package create nereus`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/catalog.html#package-apply) A Package says where it is published
- [`nereus catalog workload-type list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/catalog.html#workload-type-list) A type is a name plus answers
- [`nereus catalog check`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/catalog.html#check) A contradiction fails, a gap points
- [`nereus catalog check`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/catalog.html#check-contradiction) A contradiction fails the command

## Examples

### workload-apply

The files of catalog/ are the truth; Triton already exists and is imported the same way.

```bash
nereus catalog apply \
  --from-file catalog/
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ catalog/workloadtypes/controller created
✓ catalog/workloadtypes/service created
✓ catalog/packagetypes/cli created
✓ catalog/packagetypes/image created
✓ catalog/workloads/flux created (owner: project/nereids, type: controller)
✓ catalog/workloads/keycloak created (owner: project/nereids, type: controller)
✓ catalog/workloads/openbao created (owner: project/nereids, type: controller)
✓ catalog/workloads/triton created (owner: project/triton, type: service)
✓ catalog/packages/nereus created (owner: project/core, type: cli, registry: pypi)
✓ catalog/packages/openbao-image created (owner: project/nereids, type: image, registry: oci)

Next steps:

  nereus catalog check
```

### workload-create

No --owner: the current owner is used and named in the output.

```bash
nereus catalog workload create edge-cloudflare \
  --type controller \
  --audience none \
  --repository https://github.com/getnereus/nereus \
  --ref branch=main \
  --path controllers/edge-cloudflare/ \
  --dry-run
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
catalog/workloads/edge-cloudflare would be created (owner: project/nereids, type: controller)
Nothing changed (--dry-run).
```

### workload-list

The catalog lists what it has, one row per Workload.

```bash
nereus catalog list \
  --type service
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
WORKLOAD  ORGANIZATION  PROJECT        TYPE     AUDIENCE        STATUS
triton    getnereus     nereus/triton  service  agents, people  DeploymentNotFound
```

### workload-delete

The entry leaves the catalog; the Deployment, if any, stays.

```bash
nereus catalog delete openbao
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ catalog/workloads/openbao deleted
```

### package-apply

The same verbs, the kind in the path.

```bash
nereus catalog package create nereus \
  --project core \
  --type cli \
  --registry pypi \
  --name nereus \
  --audience people \
  --audience programs \
  --ref branch=main \
  --path cli/ \
  --dry-run
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
catalog/packages/nereus would be created (owner: project/core, type: cli, registry: pypi)
Nothing changed (--dry-run).
```

### workload-type-list

The shapes of what runs, and what each one answers.

```bash
nereus catalog workload-type list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
TYPE         RUNS    TRIGGER         STATUS
controller   always  event           Ready
function     once    request, event  Ready
job          once    schedule        Ready
service      always  request         Ready
static-site  always  request         Ready
web-app      always  request         Ready
worker       always  event           Ready
```

### check

Nereus's own catalog today: no contradiction, and each gap with its issue.

```bash
nereus catalog check
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ tenancy: 1 organization, 5 projects, every owner resolves
✓ types: every workload type and package type resolves, every registry allowed
! catalog/workloads/triton: audience people, agents, no edge reef (#470)
! catalog/workloads/triton: uses nats, no messaging reef (#576)
! catalog/packages/nereus: not found on pypi
0 contradictions, 3 gaps
```

### check-contradiction

An owner that does not exist, a registry the type does not allow, an audience missing.

```bash
nereus catalog check
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ catalog/workloads/api: owner project/ghost does not exist
✗ catalog/packages/base-image: type image takes the registries oci, not pypi
✗ catalog/workloads/worker: audience is missing
3 contradictions, 0 gaps
```

# database

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/database.md

Every command of the database Reef: a PostgreSQL per Database, owned by a node of the tenancy tree.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply database`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/database.html#reef-apply) The database Reef: one kind, Database
- [`nereus nereid apply cloudnative-pg`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/database.html#nereid-apply) The cloudnative-pg Nereid makes the Reef's default Mandate
- [`nereus database create keycloak`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/database.html#create) A Database names its owner in the tenancy tree
- [`nereus database get keycloak`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/database.html#get) Ready, with its connection in a Secret
- [`nereus database create orders`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/database.html#refused) An owner missing from the tree is refused
- [`nereus database delete keycloak`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/database.html#delete) Delete removes the Secret, then the Cluster and its volume

## Examples

### reef-apply

The release Reef with flux comes first: the Nereid releases the operator through it.

```bash
nereus reef apply database
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/database 0.1.0 created (database.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: databases)

Next steps:

  nereus database --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef database
```

### nereid-apply

CloudNativePG's operator, its chart pinned by version and SHA-256.

```bash
nereus nereid apply cloudnative-pg \
  --reef database
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/cloudnative-pg created, Ready, pinned to sha256:4908bacf6ac8: see 'nereus database --help'
  core/mandates/cloudnative-pg created (reef: database, nereid: cloudnative-pg, default)

Next steps:

  nereus database create <name> --project <name> --engine postgres
```

### create

In nereus-system, for Keycloak.

```bash
nereus database create keycloak \
  --project nereids \
  --engine postgres
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ database/databases/keycloak created (mandate: cloudnative-pg, nereid: cloudnative-pg)

Next steps:

  nereus database get keycloak
```

### get

```bash
nereus database get keycloak
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:          keycloak
Organization:  getnereus
Project:       nereus/nereids
Engine:        postgres
Mandate:       cloudnative-pg
Nereid:        cloudnative-pg
Ready:         True
Connection:    secret nereus-system/keycloak-database (host, port, dbname, username, password, uri)
```

### refused

```bash
nereus database create orders \
  --project missing \
  --engine postgres
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ database/databases/orders: owner project/missing does not exist. To fix it, run:
  nereus tenancy project list
  Nothing was changed.
```

### delete

```bash
nereus database delete keycloak \
  --dry-run
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
database/databases/keycloak deleted (dry run)
```

# delivery

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/delivery.md

Every command that takes a Workload to an Environment, and says what runs.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply delivery`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#reef-apply) The Reef, then the Nereid that delivers to Kubernetes
- [`nereus workload deploy hello@dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#workload-deploy) One command takes a Workload to an Environment
- [`nereus workload deploy hello`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#deploy-refuses) deploy never guesses the target
- [`nereus workload deploy hello@dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#deploy-build) deploy runs what a Build pushed, by its digest
- [`nereus workload deploy hello-dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#deploy-update) Every deploy is a new request, even with the same tag
- [`nereus workload deploy hello@dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#deploy-dry-run) --dry-run shows the Delivery, with the tag as typed
- [`nereus workload deploy hello@dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#deploy-wait) --wait brings the Nereid's reason to the terminal
- [`nereus workload list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#workload-list) workload list says what the catalog has
- [`nereus delivery list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#delivery-list) delivery list says what was deployed
- [`nereus delivery get hello-dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#delivery-get) delivery get says what runs and where
- [`nereus workload logs hello-dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#workload-logs) workload logs reads a Delivery by its name or its pair
- [`nereus workload deploy hello@dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#delivery-apply) A Delivery in a file resolves once
- [`nereus delivery delete hello-dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#delivery-delete) Deleting a Delivery takes the app out of the Environment
- [`nereus template render python-service`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/delivery.html#template-render) [planned #851] A template writes files, and the catalog registers them

## Examples

### reef-apply

The delivery Reef's contract.

```bash
nereus reef apply delivery \
  --from-file ./reefs/delivery/
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/delivery created (delivery.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1)
```

### workload-deploy

A Workload of the catalog, in the dev Environment.

```bash
nereus workload deploy hello@dev \
  --image registry.example.com/hello:a1b2c3d
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev created

Next steps:

  nereus delivery get hello-dev
```

### deploy-refuses

A bare name could change target in silence when a second Environment appears.

```bash
nereus workload deploy hello \
  --image registry.example.com/hello:a1b2c3d
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ deploy needs the target. To deploy hello, run:
  # to the dev Environment
  nereus workload deploy hello@dev --image registry.example.com/hello:a1b2c3d
```

### deploy-build

The image of a Build that succeeded, never a tag that may move.

```bash
nereus workload deploy hello@dev \
  --build hello-a1b2c3d
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev created

Next steps:

  nereus delivery get hello-dev
```

### deploy-update

The same tag, pushed again: the unique name works too.

```bash
nereus workload deploy hello-dev \
  --image registry.example.com/hello:a1b2c3d
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev configured

Next steps:

  nereus delivery get hello-dev
```

### deploy-dry-run

Changes nothing; the digest comes from the Nereid, after the deploy.

```bash
nereus workload deploy hello@dev \
  --image registry.example.com/hello:a1b2c3d \
  --dry-run
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
delivery/deliveries/hello-dev would be created
  workload: hello
  environment: dev
  image: registry.example.com/hello:a1b2c3d
```

### deploy-wait

A tag that does not exist fails after the Delivery is written.

```bash
nereus workload deploy hello@dev \
  --image registry.example.com/hello:does-not-exist \
  --wait
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev configured
✗ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev not ready: The registry does not have the tag does-not-exist of the repository registry.example.com/hello. To fix it, run:
  # deploy a tag that exists
  nereus workload deploy hello@dev --image registry.example.com/hello:<tag>
```

### workload-list

One row per Workload; DELIVERIES counts them, 0 means not deployed.

```bash
nereus workload list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
WORKLOAD  ORGANIZATION  PROJECT  TYPE     AUDIENCE  DELIVERIES  STATUS
billing   example       shop     service  programs  0           Ready
hello     example       hello    service  people    2           Ready

Next steps:

  nereus delivery list
```

### delivery-list

One row per Workload and Environment pair.

```bash
nereus delivery list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME         WORKLOAD  ENVIRONMENT  DIGEST         READY
hello-dev    hello     dev          sha256:9f2c1e  True
hello-stage  hello     stage        sha256:77ab40  True
```

### delivery-get

The digest running, the namespace, and the previous digest.

```bash
nereus delivery get hello-dev
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME       WORKLOAD  ENVIRONMENT  DIGEST         NAMESPACE  READY
hello-dev  hello     dev          sha256:9f2c1e  hello-dev  True

Previous digest: sha256:77ab40

Next steps:

  nereus workload logs hello-dev
```

### workload-logs

Follow what the app prints.

```bash
nereus workload logs hello-dev \
  --follow
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:53792: response:200
```

### delivery-apply

Write it as a file, then apply the file.

```bash
nereus workload deploy hello@dev \
  --image registry.example.com/hello:a1b2c3d \
  --dry-run \
  --output yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
apiVersion: delivery.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Delivery
metadata:
  name: hello-dev
```

### delivery-delete

The Workload stays in the catalog.

```bash
nereus delivery delete hello-dev
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev deleted

Next steps:

  nereus workload list
```

### template-render

The files of a new Workload, with Copier.

```bash
nereus template render python-service \
  --path ./hello \
  --param name=hello
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ catalog/templates/python-service rendered at ./hello

Next steps:

  nereus catalog apply --from-file ./hello/catalog/
```

# edge

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/edge.md

Every command of the edge Reef: domains, zones and routes, in the order a person types them.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply edge`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#apply-reef) One command applies the edge Reef, with its kinds Route, Zone and Domain
- [`nereus nereid apply cloudflare`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#apply-cloudflare) The cloudflare Nereid runs the tunnel its Mandate names
- [`nereus nereid apply godaddy`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#apply-godaddy) The godaddy Nereid talks to the registrar, through its Mandate
- [`nereus edge zone create getnereus.dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#zone-create) A zone gives the domain the nameservers that will answer for it
- [`nereus edge domain list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#domain-list-registrar) The registrar shows its domains, with the credentials asked for now and never stored
- [`nereus edge domain apply getnereus.dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#domain-apply) Nereus takes the domain and sends it to the zone's nameservers
- [`nereus edge domain list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#domain-list) The list shows the domains Nereus looks after
- [`nereus edge domain get getnereus.dev`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#domain-get) One domain shows every detail, its nameservers one per line
- [`nereus edge route create triton`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#route-hostname) A route makes a hostname reach the platform
- [`nereus edge endpoint list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#endpoint-list) The Nereids say what they serve, never where it runs
- [`nereus edge route create triton`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#route-create) A route publishes a Reef's endpoint at a fixed address
- [`nereus edge apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#apply-file) One file applies every Route and Zone, each checked before any is written
- [`nereus edge route delete triton`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#route-delete) A delete waits until its Nereid takes away what it made, unless told not to

## Examples

### apply-reef

Apply the edge Reef.

```bash
nereus reef apply edge
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/edge 0.1.0 created

Next steps:

  nereus edge --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef edge
```

### apply-cloudflare

Apply the cloudflare Nereid to the edge Reef.

```bash
nereus nereid apply cloudflare \
  --reef edge
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/cloudflare created, Ready

Next steps:

  nereus mandate create cloudflare --reef edge --nereid cloudflare --param tunnel=<tunnel> --param credentialsSecret=edge/<secret> --default
  nereus edge route create <name> --hostname <hostname>
```

### apply-godaddy

Apply the godaddy Nereid to the edge Reef.

```bash
nereus nereid apply godaddy \
  --reef edge
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/godaddy created, Ready

Next steps:

  nereus secrets create edge/godaddy --from-env key=GODADDY_KEY --from-env secret=GODADDY_SECRET
  nereus mandate create godaddy --reef edge --nereid godaddy --param credentialsSecret=edge/godaddy
  nereus edge domain list --at-registrar
```

### zone-create

Delegate the domain to the platform.

```bash
nereus edge zone create getnereus.dev \
  --mandate cloudflare
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ edge/zones/getnereus.dev created, waiting for its delegation
  nameservers: ada.ns.cloudflare.com, bob.ns.cloudflare.com
  point the registrar of getnereus.dev at them; the zone turns Active once Cloudflare sees it

Next steps:

  nereus edge zone get getnereus.dev
```

### domain-list-registrar

What the registrar holds.

```bash
nereus edge domain list \
  --at-registrar
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
GoDaddy API key:
GoDaddy API secret:
NAME           NAMESERVERS                  EXPIRES     MANAGED
example.com    ns01.domaincontrol.com (+1)  2029-10-25  no
example.org    ns01.domaincontrol.com (+1)  2028-06-11  no
getnereus.dev  ns01.domaincontrol.com (+1)  2029-10-25  no

Next steps:

  nereus edge domain get <name>
  nereus edge domain apply <name> --nameservers-from zone/<name>     # Nereus starts looking after it
```

### domain-apply

Delegate getnereus.dev to the zone.

```bash
nereus edge domain apply getnereus.dev \
  --nameservers-from zone/getnereus.dev
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ edge/domains/getnereus.dev created

Next steps:

  nereus edge domain get getnereus.dev --watch
```

### domain-list

What Nereus looks after.

```bash
nereus edge domain list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME           MANDATE  NAMESERVERS                 DELEGATED
getnereus.dev  godaddy  ada.ns.cloudflare.com (+1)  True
```

### domain-get

Every detail of one domain.

```bash
nereus edge domain get getnereus.dev
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:         getnereus.dev
Mandate:      godaddy
Delegated:    True
Expires:      2029-10-25
Nameservers:
  ada.ns.cloudflare.com
  bob.ns.cloudflare.com
  (from zone/getnereus.dev)
```

### route-hostname

Carry Triton's hostname through the tunnel.

```bash
nereus edge route create triton \
  --hostname triton.getnereus.dev
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ edge/routes/triton created, Ready: https://triton.getnereus.dev

Next steps:

  nereus edge route get triton
```

### endpoint-list

What the Nereids serve at the instance's entrance.

```bash
nereus edge endpoint list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
REEF            ENDPOINT  NEREID         PROTOCOL  PATHS                      HOSTS               PUBLISHABLE  PUBLISHED  ROUTES
authentication  realm     keycloak       http      /realms/nereus,/resources  auth.example.com    yes          no         -
rooms           mcp       triton         http      /                          triton.example.com  yes          no         -
portal          web       nereus-portal  http      /                          portal.example.com  yes          no         -
```

### route-create

Publish Triton's MCP endpoint.

```bash
nereus edge route create triton \
  --hostname triton.example.com \
  --endpoint rooms/mcp
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ edge/routes/triton created, Ready: https://triton.example.com

Next steps:

  nereus edge route get triton
```

### apply-file

Apply a file: a Zone and a Route, in the file's order.

```bash
nereus edge apply \
  --from-file edge.yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ edge/zones/example.com created
✓ edge/routes/triton created

Next steps:

  nereus edge route list
  nereus edge zone list
```

### route-delete

Delete the Route: it waits until the hostname left the tunnel.

```bash
nereus edge route delete triton
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ edge/routes/triton deleted (its Nereid took the hostname out of the tunnel)

Next steps:

  nereus edge route list
```

# environment

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/environment.md

Every command of the environment Reef: an environment per agent, made by a Nereid, gone at its expiry.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply environment`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/environment.html#setup) The environment Reef, the vcluster Nereid and its default Mandate
- [`nereus environment create a`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/environment.html#create) An environment of its own, for an hour
- [`nereus mandate create heavy`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/environment.html#size) A bigger environment, for Nereus itself
- [`nereus environment list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/environment.html#list) Two agents, two environments, and the time each one has left
- [`nereus environment kubeconfig a > a.kubeconfig`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/environment.html#kubeconfig) Its kubeconfig, read with your own credentials
- [`nereus environment delete a`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/environment.html#delete) Deleting it removes the vcluster, then its namespace
- [`nereus environment create c`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/environment.html#expires) At its expiry, its Nereid removes it by itself
- [`nereus environment create nereus`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/environment.html#nereus) The kept cluster is the environment nereus, made through its own Mandate

## Examples

### setup

The vcluster Nereid requires the release Reef: it asks it for the vcluster chart.

```bash
nereus reef apply environment
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/environment 0.1.0 created (environment.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: environments)

Next steps:

  nereus environment --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef environment
```

### create

Who it is for, and for how long.

```bash
nereus environment create a \
  --project nereus \
  --expires 1h
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ environment/environments/a created (mandate: vcluster, nereid: vcluster)

Next steps:

  nereus environment get a --watch
  nereus environment kubeconfig a
```

### size

A Mandate whose Environments are of size platform.

```bash
nereus mandate create heavy \
  --reef environment \
  --nereid vcluster \
  --param size=platform
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/mandates/heavy created (reef: environment, nereid: vcluster)

Next steps:

  nereus mandate list
```

### list

Its Nereid, its state, and when it goes.

```bash
nereus environment list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
ENVIRONMENT  ORGANIZATION  PROJECT  NEREID    STATUS  SIZE   EXPIRES
a            getnereus     nereus   vcluster  Ready   small  58m
b            getnereus     nereus   vcluster  Ready   small  58m
```

### kubeconfig

```bash
kubectl get namespaces \
  --kubeconfig a.kubeconfig
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }

default           Active   42s
kube-node-lease   Active   42s
kube-public       Active   42s
kube-system       Active   42s
```

### delete

Waits until its Nereid removed what it made.

```bash
nereus environment delete a
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
2026-10-30T19:40:35Z  … release    Deleting release/releases/env-a: Flux uninstalls the vcluster chart.
2026-10-30T19:40:36Z  · namespace  Deleting the namespace env-vcluster-a.
2026-10-30T19:40:56Z  ✓ release    release/releases/env-a deleted.
2026-10-30T19:40:56Z  … namespace  Deleting the namespace env-vcluster-a.
✓ environment/environments/a deleted

Next steps:

  nereus environment list
```

### expires

An environment for one minute.

```bash
nereus environment create c \
  --project nereus \
  --expires 1m
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ environment/environments/c created (mandate: vcluster, nereid: vcluster)

Next steps:

  nereus environment get c --watch
  nereus environment kubeconfig c
```

### nereus

The CLI's first setup registers the kept k3d cluster; vcluster stays the default.

# ideas

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/ideas.md

The owner's classified notes, served inside the cluster for Tide.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply ideas`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/ideas.html#reef-apply) The ideas Reef, with no kinds
- [`nereus nereid apply doris`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/ideas.html#nereid-apply) The doris Nereid reads the node's notes folder
- [`nereus mandate apply doris`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/ideas.html#mandate-apply) The source and the readers, then the count of notes

## Examples

### reef-apply

```bash
nereus reef apply ideas
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/ideas created (ideas.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1)

Next steps:

  nereus ideas --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef ideas
```

### nereid-apply

```bash
nereus nereid apply doris \
  --reef ideas
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/doris created, Ready, pinned to sha256:3c1d2e4f5a6b: see 'nereus ideas --help'

Next steps:

  nereus mandate apply doris --reef ideas --nereid doris --param source=/var/lib/doris/notes --param readers=ideas-readers
```

```bash
nereus mandate apply doris \
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
  nereus mandate list
```

# messaging

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/messaging.md

Every command of the messaging Reef: topics and queues, the engine under the rooms Reef.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply messaging`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/messaging.html#apply-reef) One command applies the messaging Reef and its kinds
- [`nereus nereid apply nats`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/messaging.html#apply-nats) [planned #1597] The nats Nereid looks after topics and queues
- [`nereus messaging topic create orders`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/messaging.html#topic-create) A topic carries each message to everyone who listens
- [`nereus messaging topic get orders`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/messaging.html#topic-get) One topic shows where to reach it, and delete removes it
- [`nereus messaging topic create events`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/messaging.html#topic-apply) A topic from a file: the dry run writes it, apply takes it
- [`nereus messaging queue create builds`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/messaging.html#queue-create) A queue keeps each message until one worker takes it
- [`nereus messaging queue get builds`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/messaging.html#queue-get) A queue names its stream, and delete keeps its messages
- [`nereus messaging queue create scratch`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/messaging.html#queue-apply) A queue from a file, whose delete drops its messages

## Examples

### apply-reef

Apply the messaging Reef.

```bash
nereus reef apply messaging
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/messaging 0.1.0 created (messaging.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: queues, topics)

Next steps:

  nereus messaging --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef messaging
```

### apply-nats

Apply the nats Nereid to the messaging Reef.

```bash
nereus nereid apply nats \
  --reef messaging
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/nats created, Ready, pinned to sha256:<digest>: see 'nereus messaging --help'

Next steps:

  nereus mandate create messaging-nats --reef messaging --nereid nats --match engine=nats --param jetstream=true
```

### topic-create

A topic for the orders, owned by a project.

```bash
nereus messaging topic create orders \
  --project triton \
  --engine nats
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ messaging/topics/orders created (mandate: messaging-nats, nereid: nats)

Next steps:

  nereus messaging topic get orders
```

### topic-get

Every detail of one topic.

```bash
nereus messaging topic get orders
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:             orders
Organization:     getnereus
Project:          nereus/triton
Engine:           nats
Mandate:          nats
Nereid:           nats
Deletion policy:  retain
Max age:          unlimited
Max bytes:        unlimited
Access:           shared
Ready:            True
Connection:       secret nereus-system/orders-topic (host, port, uri, subject)
```

### topic-apply

The YAML of a topic, written by a dry run.

```bash
nereus messaging topic create events \
  --project triton \
  --engine nats \
  --dry-run \
  --output yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
apiVersion: messaging.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Topic
metadata:
  name: events
spec:
  owner:
    kind: Project
    name: triton
  engine: nats
```

### queue-create

A queue for the builds to run.

```bash
nereus messaging queue create builds \
  --project triton \
  --engine nats
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ messaging/queues/builds created (mandate: messaging-nats, nereid: nats)

Next steps:

  nereus messaging queue get builds
```

### queue-get

Every detail of one queue.

```bash
nereus messaging queue get builds
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:             builds
Organization:     getnereus
Project:          nereus/triton
Engine:           nats
Mandate:          nats
Nereid:           nats
Deletion policy:  retain
Ready:            True
Connection:       secret nereus-system/builds-queue (host, port, uri, subject, stream)
```

### queue-apply

The YAML of a queue, written by a dry run.

```bash
nereus messaging queue create scratch \
  --project triton \
  --engine nats \
  --deletion-policy delete \
  --dry-run \
  --output yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
apiVersion: messaging.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Queue
metadata:
  name: scratch
spec:
  owner:
    kind: Project
    name: triton
  engine: nats
  deletionPolicy: delete
```

# notifications

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/notifications.md

Every command that tells a person something and the devices that receive it.

## Commands

- [`nereus notify "Deploy k3d-nereus?"`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/notifications.html#notify) notify is the short form agents use
- [`nereus notifications notification create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/notifications.html#notification-create) create builds a Notification from flags
- [`nereus notifications notification list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/notifications.html#notification-list) list shows what was delivered of what was asked
- [`nereus notifications subscription create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/notifications.html#subscription-create) create subscribes one of your devices from the file its browser gave
- [`nereus notifications subscription list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/notifications.html#subscription-list) list shows your own devices, never their endpoints

## Examples

### notify

Tell alice, in one line.

```bash
nereus notify "Deploy k3d-nereus?" \
  --to user/alice
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ notification n-20261122-0001 created for user/alice (kind note)

Next steps:

  nereus notifications notification get n-20261122-0001
```

### notification-create

A decision, with a title and the page it leads to.

```bash
nereus notifications notification create \
  --to user/alice \
  --title "#2078 merged" \
  --text "Deploy k3d-nereus?" \
  --kind decision \
  --url https://portal.example.com/
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ notification n-20261122-0002 created for user/alice (kind decision)

Next steps:

  nereus notifications notification get n-20261122-0002
```

### notification-list

alice's notifications: delivered over the devices it went to.

```bash
nereus notifications notification list \
  --to user/alice
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME             KIND      TITLE         DELIVERED  AGE
n-20261122-0001  note      -             0/1        5s
n-20261122-0002  decision  #2078 merged  1/1        1m
```

### subscription-create

The PushSubscription JSON, read from a file: the endpoint is never on a command line.

```bash
nereus notifications subscription create \
  --from-file push.json \
  --agent "Chrome on Android"
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ subscription s-3f2a9c created

Next steps:

  nereus notifications subscription list
```

### subscription-list

The caller's own devices.

```bash
nereus notifications subscription list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME       USER        AGENT              AGE
s-3f2a9c   user/alice  Chrome on Android  2d
```

# portal

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/portal.md

Nereus in the browser: a PWA that signs a person in and shows who they are.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply portal`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/portal.html#reef-apply) The portal Reef, with no kinds
- [`nereus nereid apply nereus-portal`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/portal.html#nereid-apply) The nereus-portal Nereid requires the authentication Reef
- [`nereus mandate apply nereus-portal`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/portal.html#mandate-apply) The publicUrl writes the HTTPRoute
- [`curl https://portal.example.com/healthz`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/portal.html#open) The PWA, its config, and the API behind the person's token

## Examples

### reef-apply

The authentication Reef and a Nereid of it come first.

```bash
nereus reef apply portal
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/portal created (portal.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1)

Next steps:

  nereus portal --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef portal
```

### nereid-apply

One process, two ports: 8080 the controller's, inside the cluster, 8081 the portal's.

```bash
nereus nereid apply nereus-portal \
  --reef portal
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/nereus-portal created, Ready, pinned to sha256:b4f9fe726220: see 'nereus portal --help'
  core/mandates/nereus-portal created (reef: portal, nereid: nereus-portal, default)

Next steps:

  nereus mandate apply nereus-portal --reef portal --nereid nereus-portal --param publicUrl=https://portal.example.com
```

### mandate-apply

The gateway parameter takes another Gateway, istio-system/ingress by default (#728).

```bash
nereus mandate apply nereus-portal \
  --reef portal \
  --nereid nereus-portal \
  --param publicUrl=https://portal.example.com
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/mandates/nereus-portal configured (reef: portal, nereid: nereus-portal, default)

Next steps:

  nereus mandate list
```

### open

Open it on a phone and install it; the login is Authorization Code with PKCE.

```bash
curl https://portal.example.com/healthz
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
ok
```

# presentations

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/presentations.md

The first slice: a deck kept by the platform, and a Session a phone drives and a room follows.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply presentations`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/presentations.html#reef-apply) The presentations Reef brings decks and sessions
- [`nereus presentations schema list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/presentations.html#schema) A deck is written anywhere, against a published schema
- [`nereus presentations presentation create storytelling`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/presentations.html#presentation-create) A deck travels as a package the platform keeps by its digest
- [`nereus presentations presentation get storytelling`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/presentations.html#presentation-export) The deck goes home as one file that opens offline
- [`nereus presentations link create storytelling`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/presentations.html#link-create) A public link opens the deck for anyone, until it expires
- [`nereus presentations session create platform-day`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/presentations.html#session-create) A Session gives the link a room follows
- [`nereus presentations session get platform-day`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/presentations.html#session-get) A Session shows its step and its link
- [`nereus presentations session list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/presentations.html#list-delete) Ending a Session frees its code

## Examples

### reef-apply

The kinds of the Reef; its Nereid, leagore, comes in #1695.

```bash
nereus reef apply presentations
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/presentations created (presentations.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: presentations, sessions)

Next steps:

  nereus presentations --help
```

### schema

The outline versions, and where the Nereus API serves each with no token.

```bash
nereus presentations schema list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
OUTLINE VERSION  URL
1                https://nereus.example.com/v1/presentations/schemas/outline/1.json
```

### presentation-create

The deck and every file it names, at most 1 MB; the object holds only its digest.

```bash
nereus presentations presentation create storytelling \
  --from talks/storytelling.yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ presentations/presentations/storytelling created, revision 1 (sha256:3f9c2a71)
  copied 8 references and 1 file from outside the folder, origin recorded

Next steps:

  nereus presentations session create <name> --presentation storytelling --talk 30m
```

### presentation-export

The latest revision, with its notes, as one self-contained HTML file.

```bash
nereus presentations presentation get storytelling \
  --output html
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ storytelling.html written (revision sha256:3f9c2a71, opens offline)
```

### link-create

A link anyone can open for thirty days, no login.

```bash
nereus presentations link create storytelling \
  --expires 30d
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ presentations/presentations/storytelling link created
  public: https://nereus.example.com/d/9FK2PQ7XMZ4HR8TV3WKN6PQ2JD (expires 2026-12-17)

Next steps:

  nereus presentations link delete storytelling
```

### session-create

A talk of thirty minutes, on the revision fixed now.

```bash
nereus presentations session create platform-day \
  --presentation storytelling \
  --talk 30m
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ presentations/sessions/platform-day created (revision sha256:3f9c2a71)
  follow: https://nereus.example.com/p/K7Q4

Next steps:

  nereus presentations session get platform-day
```

### session-get

The step is the Nereid's live one; the followers count arrives with the follow stream (#1696).

```bash

```

``` { .text .output title="output" }

```

### list-delete

Every Session.

```bash
nereus presentations session list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME          PRESENTATION  TALK  CODE  STEP  AGE
platform-day  storytelling  30m   K7Q4  0/24  5m
```

# registry

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/registry.md

Every command that runs an image registry in the cluster and publishes to it.

## Commands

- [`nereus registry create main`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/registry.html#registry-create) create asks for a registry, and names who makes it
- [`nereus registry create main`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/registry.html#registry-create-exists) create fails when it exists, and lists what to run
- [`nereus registry get main`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/registry.html#registry-get) get gives the address an image reference uses
- [`nereus registry list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/registry.html#registry-list) list shows every registry, one line each
- [`nereus registry apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/registry.html#registry-apply) apply takes files, and waits for the Nereid
- [`nereus registry delete main`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/registry.html#registry-delete) delete removes the registry and what its Nereid made
- [`nereus registry create main`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/registry.html#registry-purge) A registry purges, when set, the images no Delivery runs
- [`nereus registry repository publish hello`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/registry.html#repository-publish) publish pushes an image with the platform's credential

## Examples

### registry-create

A registry, through the Reef's default Mandate.

```bash
nereus registry create main
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
secrets/vaults/registries created
registry/registries/main created (mandate: zot, nereid: zot)

Next steps:

  nereus registry get main
```

### registry-create-exists

The same name twice.

```bash
nereus registry create main
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ registry/registries/main already exists. To change it, run:
  # write it as a file, then apply the file
  nereus registry create main --dry-run --output yaml > main.yaml
  nereus registry apply --from-file main.yaml
```

### registry-get

Who runs it, the address to pull from, and whether it is ready.

```bash
nereus registry get main
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME  NEREID  PURGE  PULL-ADDRESS     READY
main  zot     168h   localhost:31874  True

credential: secret registries/main-pull (vault registries)

localhost:31874 is a NodePort, for an image reference on this cluster's nodes. Reading it takes the credential above.

Next steps:

  nereus registry repository publish hello --registry main --image hello:v1
```

### registry-list

Every registry, in alphabetical order.

```bash
nereus registry list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME  NEREID  PURGE  PULL-ADDRESS     READY
main  zot     168h   localhost:31874  True

Next steps:

  nereus registry get main
```

### registry-apply

Create or update from a file or a folder, and return at once.

```bash
nereus registry apply \
  --from-file main.yaml \
  --wait false
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
registry/registries/main created

Next steps:

  nereus registry list
```

### registry-delete

Delete it, and wait until it is gone.

```bash
nereus registry delete main
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
registry/registries/main deleted

Next steps:

  nereus registry list
```

### registry-purge

A registry that deletes the images no Delivery runs, a week after they were built.

```bash
nereus registry create main \
  --purge-unused 168h
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
registry/registries/main created (mandate: zot, nereid: zot; purge: images no Delivery runs, after 168h)

Next steps:

  nereus registry get main
```

### repository-publish

The first tag of a repository.

```bash
nereus registry repository publish hello \
  --registry main \
  --image hello:v1
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
registry/registries/main/repositories/hello created
registry/registries/main/repositories/hello/tags/v1 published (sha256:ab12…)

Next steps:

  kubectl run hello --image localhost:31874/hello:v1
```

# release

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/release.md

Every command of the release Reef: where a chart comes from, what it is, where it goes and the release itself.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply release`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#apply-reef) One command applies the release Reef, with its four kinds
- [`nereus nereid apply reference-release`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#apply-reference) The reference-release Nereid answers every kind with no tool, through the reference Mandate
- [`nereus nereid apply flux`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#apply-flux) The flux Nereid installs Flux and becomes the default through its Mandate
- [`nereus release repository create codecentric`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#repository-create) A repository says where the charts come from
- [`nereus release repository create codecentric`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#repository-apply) Apply takes a file, and applying what already holds changes nothing
- [`nereus release repository list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#repository-list) The list shows every repository and whether it is ready
- [`nereus release repository get codecentric`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#repository-get) One repository, by its name
- [`nereus release repository delete codecentric`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#repository-delete) A repository goes once no source names it
- [`nereus release source create keycloak`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#source-create) A source is one chart of a repository, at one version
- [`nereus release source create keycloak`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#source-apply) A new version is one file away
- [`nereus release source list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#source-list) The list shows every source with its chart and version
- [`nereus release source get keycloak`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#source-get) One source, by its name
- [`nereus release repository create ghcr`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#source-publish) Publishing goes through the platform, with its credential, never yours
- [`nereus release source delete keycloak`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#source-delete) A source in use is refused, with what to delete first
- [`nereus release target create dev-identity`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#target-create) A target is a namespace, of an environment or of the cluster Nereus runs in
- [`nereus release target create dev-identity`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#target-apply) Applying the same target again changes nothing
- [`nereus release target list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#target-list) The list shows every target with its environment and namespace
- [`nereus release target get dev-identity`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#target-get) One target, by its name
- [`nereus release target delete dev-identity`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#target-delete) A target goes once no release names it
- [`nereus release create keycloak-reference`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#release-create) A release runs a source in a target, through the Reef's default Mandate
- [`nereus release create keycloak`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#release-create-values) Values and a Mandate of your choice, with Flux installing the chart
- [`nereus release create keycloak`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#release-create-secrets) A release asks for its secrets by name, and its values never pass through Nereus
- [`nereus release create keycloak-reference`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#release-apply) One folder holds the whole release, and the second apply changes nothing
- [`nereus release list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#release-list) The list shows every release, its version and the Nereid behind it
- [`nereus release get keycloak-reference`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#release-get) One release, by its name
- [`nereus release delete keycloak-reference`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#release-delete) Deleting a release uninstalls its chart
- [`kubectl apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#ingress-crds) The Gateway API CRDs come first, applied by hand for now
- [`nereus release repository create istio`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#ingress-repository) Istio's charts come from its own Helm repository
- [`nereus release source create istio-base`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#ingress-sources) Three charts at one pinned version: base and istiod first
- [`nereus release source create istio-gateway`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#ingress-sources-gateway) Three charts at one pinned version: then the gateway, into istio-system
- [`nereus release create istio-base`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#ingress-istio-base) Each chart starts once the previous one is Ready: base first
- [`nereus release create istiod`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#ingress-istiod) Then istiod, the control plane
- [`nereus release create istio-gateway`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#ingress-istio-gateway) Last, the ingress gateway, with no values of its own
- [`kubectl apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/release.html#ingress-curl) A Gateway opens Envoy's listener, and with no route it answers 404

## Examples

### apply-reef

Apply the release Reef.

```bash
nereus reef apply release
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/release 0.1.0 created (release.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: releases, repositories, sources, targets)

Next steps:

  nereus release --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef release
```

### apply-reference

Apply the reference Nereid to the release Reef.

```bash
nereus nereid apply reference-release \
  --reef release \
  --image localhost:5111/reference-release-controller:0.1.0
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/reference-release created, Ready, pinned to sha256:b3c32d74194e: see 'nereus release --help'

Next steps:

  nereus nereid list
```

### apply-flux

Apply the flux Nereid to the release Reef.

```bash
nereus nereid apply flux \
  --reef release
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/flux created, Ready, pinned to sha256:e8731e3fb833: see 'nereus release --help'
  flux/v2.9.6 created (source-controller, helm-controller in namespace flux-system)

Next steps:

  nereus mandate create flux --reef release --nereid flux --default
```
