# rooms

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/rooms.md

Every command of the rooms Reef: rooms, peers and the agents' sessions, on a Topic of the messaging Reef.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply rooms`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#apply-reef) One command applies the rooms Reef and its kinds
- [`nereus nereid apply triton`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#apply-triton) The triton Nereid looks after rooms and peers
- [`nereus rooms create ops`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#room-create) A room is created by name, and its Topic comes with it
- [`nereus rooms list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#room-list) One room shows whose it is and the peers in it
- [`nereus rooms create platform`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#room-apply) A room from a file: the dry run writes it, apply takes it
- [`nereus rooms delete platform`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#room-delete) Deleting a room keeps its messages, unless it says otherwise
- [`nereus rooms peer list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#peer-list) Every agent's session in the rooms is a Peer
- [`nereus rooms peer get ana.doto`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#peer-get) One Peer says whose agent it is, and which rooms it is in
- [`nereus rooms join ops`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#join) A coding agent joins a room with your own login
- [`nereus rooms leave billing`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#leave) A session leaves one room, and stays in the others
- [`nereus rooms session list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#session-list) Each room session, from the first peer in to the last one out
- [`nereus rooms session get ops-20261122-1002`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#session-get) One room session says who came and went, and when
- [`nereus rooms follow`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#follow) A person follows the room where the agents talk
- [`nereus rooms pull doto`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#pull) A hook pulls each room's new messages into the session
- [`nereus rooms post "k3d-nereus is mine until 21:30"`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#post) A person posts to the room, as the agents do
- [`nereus order create "run make checks"`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/rooms.html#orders) [idea] An order goes to one idle agent, and the list follows it

## Examples

### apply-reef

Apply the rooms Reef.

```bash
nereus reef apply rooms
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/rooms 0.1.0 created (rooms.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: peers, rooms, roomsessions)

Next steps:

  nereus rooms --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef rooms
```

### apply-triton

Apply the triton Nereid to the rooms Reef.

```bash
nereus nereid apply triton \
  --reef rooms
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/triton created, Ready, pinned to sha256:<digest>: see 'nereus rooms --help'

Next steps:

  nereus rooms create <name>
```

### room-create

A room for the operations peers.

```bash
nereus rooms create ops \
  --project payments \
  --description "Operations peers"
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ rooms/rooms/ops created (owner: project/payments)

Next steps:

  nereus rooms get ops
```

### room-list

The rooms of the Reef.

```bash
nereus rooms list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME    ORGANIZATION  PROJECT   PEERS  MESSAGES  LAST MESSAGE  AGE
nereus  example       -         3      -         -             12d
ops     example       payments  2      -         -             1m
```

### room-apply

The YAML of a room, written by a dry run.

```bash
nereus rooms create platform \
  --project payments \
  --description "Platform peers" \
  --dry-run \
  --output yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
apiVersion: rooms.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Room
metadata:
  name: platform
spec:
  owner:
    kind: Project
    name: payments
  description: Platform peers
```

### room-delete

Remove the room: its Topic goes with it.

```bash
nereus rooms delete platform \
  --yes
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ rooms/rooms/platform deleted (deletionPolicy: retain, its messages are kept)

Next steps:

  nereus rooms list
```

### peer-list

The peers of the Reef.

```bash
nereus rooms peer list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME      ROOMS  PHASE  SINCE
ana.doto  ops    Ready  10:02:11
```

### peer-get

Every detail of one peer.

```bash
nereus rooms peer get ana.doto
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:   ana.doto
Owner:  User/ana
Agent:  doto
Tool:   claude-code
Rooms:  ops
Phase:  Ready
Since:  10:02:11
```

### join

Open Claude Code with an agent in the room ops.

```bash
nereus rooms join ops
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
no name given: the agent is doto (a Nereid's name, free on Triton)
  peer: rooms/peers/alice.doto in ops
  wake: a message to doto or an ask to the room wakes this session (channel nereus-local)
starting doto with claude-code: in the room ops on Triton
```

### leave

From inside the session: leave the room billing.

```bash
nereus rooms leave billing
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ doto left the room billing
```

### session-list

The room sessions.

```bash
nereus rooms session list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME               ROOM  PEERS  MESSAGES  STARTED   ENDED
ops-20261122-1002  ops   2      37        10:02:11  11:40:05
ops-20261122-1415  ops   1      -         14:15:30  -
```

### session-get

One room session.

```bash
nereus rooms session get ops-20261122-1002
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
room: ops
started: 2026-11-22T10:02:11Z
ended: 2026-11-22T11:40:05Z
peers:
  ana.doto    joined 10:02:11  left 11:40:05
  bruno.eione joined 10:05:43  left 11:31:12
messages: 37 (sequences 1204..1240)
```

### follow

Follow the room nereus, until Ctrl-C.

```bash
nereus rooms follow \
  --room nereus
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
21:02:11  alice/speo  claim    #1406 in ../nereus-1406-size, paths controllers/vcluster/
21:02:40  bob/doto    note     k3d-nereus is mine until 21:30
21:30:02  bob/doto    release  k3d-nereus
```

### pull

What a session's hook runs: the new messages for agent doto.

```bash
nereus rooms pull doto
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit", "additionalContext": "[note] bob/doto: k3d-nereus is mine until 21:30"}}
```

### post

Tell the room the cluster is taken.

```bash
nereus rooms post "k3d-nereus is mine until 21:30" \
  --room nereus
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ rooms/rooms/nereus note posted (id m-20261122-0128)
```

### orders

Send an order to agent m15.

```bash
nereus order create "run make checks" \
  --agent m15
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ order/20261030-142549-4dae created, sent to m15
```

# scm

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/scm.md

Every command that lets Nereus reach a source host as an application, never as a person.

## Commands

- [`nereus nereid apply github`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/scm.html#apply-github) One github Nereid serves both Reefs, opt-in
- [`nereus scm connection create example`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/scm.html#connection-create) A Connection names an organisation, and nothing secret
- [`nereus scm connection list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/scm.html#connection-list) list says what each App reaches, and what is missing
- [`nereus scm connection delete labs`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/scm.html#connection-delete) delete removes the Connection, never the App
- [`nereus nereid apply forgejo`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/scm.html#mirror-apply) The forgejo Nereid runs Forgejo in the cluster, in the profile
- [`nereus scm mirror create nereus`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/scm.html#mirror-create) A Mirror copies a repository into the cluster
- [`nereus scm mirror list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/scm.html#mirror-list) list shows the commit each copy holds

## Examples

### apply-github

Apply the github Nereid to both Reefs.

```bash
nereus nereid apply github \
  --reef authentication \
  --reef scm
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/github created, Ready, pinned to sha256:1e74cbc6a968: see 'nereus authentication --help'
  namespaces/nereus-system-github applied (the github Nereid's Role there, where vault default delivers the App keys)

Next steps:

  nereus mandate create github --reef authentication --nereid github --param appId=<id> --param privateKey=<secret> --param allow=<namespace>:<repository>:<permission>=<level> --default
  nereus mandate create github-scm --reef scm --nereid github --param identity=github --default
```

### connection-create

The organisation, through the Reef's default Mandate.

```bash
nereus scm connection create example \
  --org example
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ scm/connections/example created (mandate github-scm)

Next steps:

  nereus scm connection get example
```

### connection-list

Every Connection, with its status.

```bash
nereus scm connection list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
CONNECTION  ORG           MANDATE     STATUS              DEFAULT
example     example       github-scm  Ready               yes
labs        example-labs  github-scm  NotInstalled        no
meta        example-meta  github-scm  MissingPermissions  no
some        example-some  github-scm  NotAllRepositories  no
```

### connection-delete

Remove the Connection.

```bash
nereus scm connection delete labs
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ scm/connections/labs deleted

Next steps:

  nereus scm connection list
```

### mirror-apply

Apply the forgejo Nereid to the scm Reef; it needs the release and secrets Reefs.

```bash
nereus nereid apply forgejo \
  --reef scm
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/nereids/forgejo created, Ready: see 'nereus scm --help'
  core/mandates/forgejo created (reef: scm, nereid: forgejo)

Next steps:

  nereus scm mirror create <name> --from https://github.com/<owner>/<repository>
```

### mirror-create

Copy a public repository, pulled every 10 minutes.

```bash
nereus scm mirror create nereus \
  --from https://github.com/getnereus/nereus \
  --interval 10m
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ scm/mirrors/nereus created (mandate forgejo)

Next steps:

  nereus scm mirror get nereus
```

### mirror-list

Every Mirror, the commit it holds and its status.

```bash
nereus scm mirror list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
MIRROR   FROM                                       MANDATE  LAST SYNC             COMMIT   STATUS
nereus   https://github.com/getnereus/nereus        forgejo  2026-11-10T12:00:00Z  68d7a0d  Ready
outside  https://example.com/example/outside        forgejo  -                     -        SourceUnreachable
```

# secrets

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/secrets.md

Every command of the secrets Reef: vaults, and the secrets in them, encrypted before they leave the machine.

## Commands

- [`nereus init`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#init) The profile brings the secrets Reef ready to use, with its key and the vault default
- [`nereus secrets create google-oauth`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#create) A secret is encrypted on your machine, before it leaves it
- [`nereus secrets create google-oauth`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#create-exists) Creating it again is refused, with how to change it
- [`nereus secrets create github-app`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#create-file) A key can come from a file, such as a private key
- [`nereus secrets create google-oauth`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#apply) Apply takes a folder of secrets, and the second apply changes nothing
- [`nereus secrets list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#list) The list shows every secret with its keys, never a value
- [`nereus secrets get default/google-oauth`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#get) One secret, by its vault and name
- [`nereus secrets get google-oauth`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#get-yaml) As YAML, the object shows the names of its keys instead of the envelopes
- [`nereus secrets vault list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#vault-list) The list shows every vault, its Nereid and how many secrets it holds
- [`nereus secrets vault create team-a`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#vault-create) A vault for a team, with the namespaces allowed to bind its secrets
- [`nereus secrets vault delete default`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#vault-delete-held) A vault that holds secrets is refused, with what to delete first
- [`nereus secrets delete default/google-oauth`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#delete) A secret goes by its full name, or by its name in the vault default
- [`nereus secrets vault delete team-a`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#vault-delete) An empty vault goes
- [`nereus secrets binding create keycloak-google`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#binding-create) A binding makes a Kubernetes Secret from a secret, in a namespace the vault allows
- [`nereus secrets binding create payments`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#binding-refused) A namespace the vault does not allow, or a key the secret does not have, is refused before anything is written
- [`cat test/charts/binding-demo/templates/secretbinding.yaml`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#binding-chart) A chart asks for its secret with a SecretBinding among its templates
- [`nereus secrets binding list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#binding-list) Every binding, with who asked for it
- [`nereus secrets get default/google-oauth`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#binding-used) A secret says where it is used, and is not deleted while it is
- [`nereus secrets binding delete keycloak-google`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/secrets.html#binding-delete) A binding goes, and its Kubernetes Secret with it

## Examples

### init

Install core and the internal developer platform profile.

```bash
nereus init \
  --profile internal-developer-platform
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ reef secrets              0.0s  core/reefs/secrets 0.1.0 created (secrets.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: secrets, secretbindings, vaults)
✓ nereid openbao           21.5s  core/nereids/openbao created, Ready
✓ mandate default           0.0s  core/mandates/default created (reef: secrets, nereid: openbao, default)
✓ public key                5.0s  rsa-4096, SHA256:yJi61pETATOGjDo6b6B2y5+V8jiPPDruqOUYp2CtPFs, version 1
✓ vault default             0.1s  secrets/vaults/default created (mandate: default)
```

### create

Two keys, each from an environment variable.

```bash
nereus secrets create google-oauth \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth created (key SHA256:GQ8TrJ9h6ZrNYHItBycWK+tXkURjowfJWcjEyabRIKI)
Stored encrypted; a Kubernetes Secret is made only when a binding asks for it (#532).

Next steps:

  nereus secrets get default/google-oauth
```

### create-exists

Create it again.

```bash
nereus secrets create google-oauth \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth already exists. To change it, write it as a file, then apply the file:
  nereus secrets create google-oauth --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID --dry-run --output yaml > google-oauth.yaml
  nereus secrets apply --from-file google-oauth.yaml
```

### create-file

A private key from a file, and an id from the environment.

```bash
nereus secrets create github-app \
  --vault default \
  --from-file private-key=key.pem \
  --from-env APP_ID
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/github-app created (key SHA256:GQ8TrJ9h6ZrNYHItBycWK+tXkURjowfJWcjEyabRIKI)
Stored encrypted; a Kubernetes Secret is made only when a binding asks for it (#532).

Next steps:

  nereus secrets get default/github-app
```

### apply

Apply the folder.

```bash
nereus secrets apply \
  --from-file secrets
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/github-app configured
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth configured

Next steps:

  nereus secrets list
```

### list

Every secret.

```bash
nereus secrets list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
VAULT    NAME          KEYS                  STATUS  AGE
default  github-app    APP_ID, +1            Ready   4s
default  google-oauth  GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, +1  Ready   5s
```

### get

One secret.

```bash
nereus secrets get default/google-oauth
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Vault     default
Name      google-oauth
Keys      GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
          GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
Version   2
Location  openbao: secret/nereus/default/google-oauth
Bindings  -
Status    Ready
Age       10s
```

### get-yaml

The object, without its values.

```bash
nereus secrets get google-oauth \
  --output yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
apiVersion: secrets.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: default.google-oauth
  namespace: nereus-system
spec:
  vault: default
  keys:
  - GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
  - GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
status:
  location: 'openbao: secret/nereus/default/google-oauth'
  mandate: default
  nereid: openbao
  phase: Ready
  version: '2'
```

### vault-list

Every vault.

```bash
nereus secrets vault list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME     NEREID   NAMESPACES     SECRETS  STATUS  AGE
default  openbao  nereus-system  2        Ready   4m
```

### vault-create

A vault the identity and tools namespaces may bind.

```bash
nereus secrets vault create team-a \
  --allow-namespace identity \
  --allow-namespace tools
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/team-a created

Next steps:

  nereus secrets create <secret> --vault team-a --from-env <VAR>
```

### vault-delete-held

The vault default still holds two secrets.

```bash
nereus secrets vault delete default
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ secrets/vaults/default holds secrets github-app, google-oauth. Delete them first:
  nereus secrets delete default/github-app
  nereus secrets delete default/google-oauth
```

### delete

By vault and name.

```bash
nereus secrets delete default/google-oauth
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth deleted

Next steps:

  nereus secrets list
```

### vault-delete

Delete the vault team-a.

```bash
nereus secrets vault delete team-a
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/team-a deleted

Next steps:

  nereus secrets vault list
```

### binding-create

Keycloak, in the namespace identity, reads the Google client under its own key names.

```bash
nereus secrets binding create keycloak-google \
  --secret default/google-oauth \
  --namespace identity \
  --key client-id=GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID \
  --key client-secret=GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth/secretbindings/identity/keycloak-google created
Secret keycloak-google ready in namespace identity.

Next steps:

  nereus secrets binding get keycloak-google --namespace identity
```

### binding-refused

The vault default does not allow the namespace payments.

```bash
nereus secrets binding create payments \
  --secret default/google-oauth \
  --namespace payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ secrets/vaults/default does not allow namespace payments (it allows: nereus-system, identity, tools).
  Allow it: write the vault as a file, add payments to spec.allowedNamespaces, then apply the file:
  nereus secrets vault get default --output yaml > default.yaml
  nereus secrets vault apply --from-file default.yaml
```

### binding-chart

The template of test/charts/binding-demo.

```bash
cat test/charts/binding-demo/templates/secretbinding.yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
apiVersion: {{ .Values.apiGroup }}/v1alpha1
kind: SecretBinding
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
  labels:
    {{- include "binding-demo.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  secret: {{ required "secret is <vault>/<secret>" .Values.secret | quote }}
```

### binding-list

In every namespace.

```bash
nereus secrets binding list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME             SECRET                NAMESPACE  FOR                 STATUS  AGE
keycloak-google  default/google-oauth  identity   system:admin        Ready   12s
binding-demo     default/google-oauth  tools      chart binding-demo  Ready   4s
```

### binding-used

The secret lists its bindings.

```bash
nereus secrets get default/google-oauth
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Vault     default
Name      google-oauth
Keys      GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
          GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
Version   2
Location  openbao: secret/nereus/default/google-oauth
Bindings  identity/keycloak-google  by system:admin        Ready
          tools/binding-demo        by chart binding-demo  Ready
Status    Ready
Age       30s
```

### binding-delete

The binding keycloak-google.

```bash
nereus secrets binding delete keycloak-google \
  --namespace identity
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth/secretbindings/identity/keycloak-google deleted

Next steps:

  nereus secrets binding list --namespace identity
```

# teams

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/teams.md

Every command of the first slice: teams on the tenancy tree, their members and positions.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply teams`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#reef-apply) The teams Reef brings teams and members
- [`nereus teams create payments`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#team-create) A team sits on a node of the tenancy tree
- [`nereus teams create billing`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#team-missing-owner) A team whose owner does not exist is refused
- [`nereus teams member create ana`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#member-lead) Ana joins as the tech lead: a position
- [`nereus teams member create bruno`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#member-developer) Bruno joins with no position
- [`nereus teams get payments`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#team-get) The team shows its members and positions
- [`nereus teams list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#team-list) Every team, its owner and how many members
- [`nereus teams delete payments`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#team-delete-refused) A team with members is not deleted
- [`nereus teams member delete bruno`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#member-delete) Bruno leaves the team
- [`nereus teams apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/teams.html#team-apply) A file of teams and members, applied again with no change

## Examples

### reef-apply

The kinds of the Reef, with no Nereid.

```bash
nereus reef apply teams
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/teams created (teams.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: members, teams)

Next steps:

  nereus teams --help
```

### team-create

The team of the payments Project.

```bash
nereus teams create payments \
  --project payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ teams/teams/payments created

Next steps:

  nereus teams member create <user> --team payments
```

### team-missing-owner

No Project billing yet.

```bash
nereus teams create billing \
  --project billing
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ teams/teams/billing: its owner project/billing does not exist: see 'nereus tenancy project list'
```

### member-lead

A member with a position.

```bash
nereus teams member create ana \
  --team payments \
  --position tech-lead
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ teams/teams/payments/members/ana created

Next steps:

  nereus teams get payments
```

### member-developer

A member like most.

```bash
nereus teams member create bruno \
  --team payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ teams/teams/payments/members/bruno created

Next steps:

  nereus teams get payments
```

### team-get

Who is in the team.

```bash
nereus teams get payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
payments: 2 members, owner project/payments
MEMBER  POSITION   USER
ana     tech-lead  core/users/ana
bruno   -          core/users/bruno

Next steps:

  nereus authorization binding create <name> --role <role> --team payments --project payments
```

### team-list

The teams of the platform.

```bash
nereus teams list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
NAME      ORGANIZATION  PROJECT   MEMBERS  AGE
payments  example       payments  2        5m
```

### team-delete-refused

Two members still in it.

```bash
nereus teams delete payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ teams/teams/payments has 2 members (ana, bruno): delete them first:
  nereus teams member delete ana --team payments
  Nothing was changed.
```

### member-delete

The team keeps its other members.

```bash
nereus teams member delete bruno \
  --team payments
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ teams/teams/payments/members/bruno deleted

Next steps:

  nereus teams get payments
```

### team-apply

Teams first, then their members.

```bash
nereus teams apply \
  --from-file payments.yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ teams/teams/payments created
✓ teams/teams/payments/members/ana created
✓ teams/teams/payments/members/bruno created

Next steps:

  nereus teams list
```

# tenancy

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/tenancy.md

Every command of the tenancy Reef: whose a thing is, as a tree of Organizations and Projects.

## Commands

- [`nereus reef apply tenancy`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#reef-apply) The tenancy Reef, with the kinds of this instance
- [`nereus status`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#status) No Nereid by design: the tenancy Reef is Ready with none
- [`nereus tenancy organization create example`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#organization-create) Another boundary: an Organization, the root of its tree
- [`nereus tenancy project create shop`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#project-create) A Project under the Organization, the path from the root
- [`nereus tenancy project create checkout`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#project-nested) A Project under another Project
- [`nereus tenancy project list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#project-list) Each Project with its parent, the path only in get
- [`nereus tenancy project get checkout`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#project-get) One Project in full: its path and its boundary
- [`nereus tenancy apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#apply) Nereus's own tree, from files, parents before children
- [`nereus tenancy project delete shop`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#delete) A node with children waits for them
- [`nereus tenancy project delete shop`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#delete-cascade) A node and everything under it, deepest first
- [`nereus config set owner project/triton`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/tenancy.html#config-owner) The current owner in the CLI's config, so --owner is optional

## Examples

### reef-apply

The CRDs of this instance, from its reefs/tenancy/.

```bash
nereus reef apply tenancy \
  --from-file reefs/tenancy/
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ core/reefs/tenancy created (tenancy.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: organizations, projects)

Next steps:

  nereus tenancy organization create <organization>
```

### status

Right after a plain init: core, and the tenancy Reef every profile applies.

```bash
nereus status
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
REEF     NEREID      VERSION  STATUS  AGE
core     nereus-api  0.1.0    Ready   2m
tenancy  -           -        Ready   2m
```

### organization-create

The kind with the boundary annotation takes no parent.

```bash
nereus tenancy organization create example
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ tenancy/organizations/example created

Next steps:

  nereus tenancy organization list
```

### project-create

A repository, under the Organization.

```bash
nereus tenancy project create shop \
  --parent organization/example \
  --repository https://github.com/example/shop
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ tenancy/organizations/example/projects/shop created

Next steps:

  nereus tenancy project list
```

### project-nested

A part of the shop, inside it.

```bash
nereus tenancy project create checkout \
  --parent project/shop
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ tenancy/organizations/example/projects/shop/projects/checkout created

Next steps:

  nereus tenancy project list
```

### project-list

One row per Project, in the tree's order.

```bash
nereus tenancy project list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
ORGANIZATION  PROJECT         REPOSITORY
example       shop            https://github.com/example/shop
example       shop/checkout   -
getnereus     nereus          https://github.com/getnereus/nereus
getnereus     nereus/core     -
getnereus     nereus/docs     -
getnereus     nereus/nereids  -
getnereus     nereus/triton   -
```

### project-get

The path climbs spec.parent to the root.

```bash
nereus tenancy project get checkout
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Name:        checkout
Kind:        Project
Path:        tenancy/organizations/example/projects/shop/projects/checkout
Parent:      project/shop
Boundary:    organization/example
Repository:  -
```

### apply

The Organization and the Projects of this repository, in tenancy/: init wrote them.

```bash
nereus tenancy apply \
  --from-file tenancy/
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
tenancy/organizations/getnereus unchanged
tenancy/organizations/getnereus/projects/nereus unchanged
tenancy/organizations/getnereus/projects/nereus/projects/core unchanged
tenancy/organizations/getnereus/projects/nereus/projects/docs unchanged
tenancy/organizations/getnereus/projects/nereus/projects/nereids unchanged
tenancy/organizations/getnereus/projects/nereus/projects/triton unchanged

Next steps:

  nereus tenancy --help
```

### delete

A Project with a child is refused.

```bash
nereus tenancy project delete shop
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✗ tenancy/organizations/example/projects/shop has 1 child (checkout): delete it first, or it with it:
  nereus tenancy project delete shop --cascade --dry-run
  Nothing was changed.
```

### delete-cascade

First what it would delete.

```bash
nereus tenancy project delete shop \
  --cascade \
  --dry-run
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
tenancy/organizations/example/projects/shop/projects/checkout deleted (dry run)
tenancy/organizations/example/projects/shop deleted (dry run)
```

### config-owner

The node the next commands are for.

```bash
nereus config set owner project/triton
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ config: owner = project/triton
```

# usage

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/usage.md

Every command that reports a coding agent's quota window and shows where it is heading.

## Commands

- [`nereus usage report weekly`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/usage.html#usage-report) report sends a reading, read now
- [`nereus usage report weekly`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/usage.html#usage-replace) --replace says the share really went down
- [`nereus usage report weekly`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/usage.html#usage-offline) offline, report keeps the reading locally and get answers from it
- [`nereus usage apply`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/usage.html#usage-apply) apply writes the windows of a file, under the same rules
- [`nereus usage get weekly`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/usage.html#usage-get) get shows the forecast at the reset, today's goal and the week day by day
- [`nereus usage dayoff create 2026-11-10`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/usage.html#usage-dayoff) A day off leaves a date out of the figures
- [`nereus usage workweek create`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/usage.html#usage-workweek) The work week leaves the weekdays not worked out, and get marks every day off
- [`nereus usage list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/reefs/usage.html#usage-list-delete) list shows every window, delete forgets one

## Examples

### usage-report

75% used, resetting on Monday at 01:00 in São Paulo.

```bash
nereus usage report weekly \
  --used 75 \
  --resets-at 2026-11-16T01:00:00-03:00
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ usage/windows/weekly reported (75% used, resets Mon 16/11 01:00)

Next steps:

  nereus usage get weekly
```

### usage-replace

The usage was reset mid-week: 98% kept, 91% now.

```bash
nereus usage report weekly \
  --used 91 \
  --resets-at 2026-11-16T01:00:00-03:00 \
  --replace
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ usage/windows/weekly replaced 98% (91% used, resets Mon 16/11 01:00), forecast 110.7% slow

Next steps:

  nereus usage get weekly
```

### usage-offline

Nereus unreachable: the reading goes to the local cache.

```bash
nereus usage report weekly \
  --used 75 \
  --resets-at 2026-11-16T01:00:00-03:00
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ usage/windows/weekly kept locally (75% used, resets Mon 16/11 01:00): Nereus unreachable, next try in 5m

Next steps:

  nereus usage get weekly
```

### usage-apply

A file of UsageWindows, or a folder of them.

```bash
nereus usage apply \
  --from-file weekly.yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ usage/windows/weekly created

Next steps:

  nereus usage list
```

### usage-get

The times in the window's time zone.

```bash
nereus usage get weekly
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
WINDOW  USED  RESETS           FORECAST  PACE    TODAY  READ
weekly  75%   Mon 16/11 01:00  91%       steady  ≤75%   Sat 19:06

DAY        TOTAL  ADJUSTED  GAP  ALLOWED  SPENT
Mon 09/11  10%    11%       -1   +9%      +10%
Tue 10/11  ~21%   21%       ±0   +11%     ~+11%
Wed 11/11  31%    36%       -5   +15%     +10%
Thu 12/11  41%    42%       -1   +11%     +10%
Fri 13/11  60%    56%       +4   +15%     +19%
Sat 14/11  75%    70%       +5   +15%     +15%   today, goal 75%
Sun 15/11  ~91%   100%      -9   +25%     ~+13%  plan
```

### usage-dayoff

A sick day, marked after it passed.

```bash
nereus usage dayoff create 2026-11-10 \
  --reason Sick
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ usage/dayoffs/2026-11-10 created
```

### usage-workweek

Weekends off.

```bash
nereus usage workweek create \
  --off sat=Weekend \
  --off sun=Weekend
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ usage/workweek created
```

### usage-list-delete

The same columns as get.

```bash
nereus usage list
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
WINDOW  USED  RESETS           FORECAST  PACE    TODAY  READ
weekly  75%   Mon 16/11 01:00  91%       steady  ≤79%   Sat 19:06
```

# The settings file

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/settings.md

The file `~/.config/nereus/init.yaml` holds the settings of [`nereus init`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#init): written once with `--generate-file`, read by every plain `nereus init`.

A setting comes from its flag, else from the file, else from its default, in that order. An unknown key is an error.

## The file

Two YAML documents, written by `nereus init --generate-file`: an `InitConfig`, how to build the platform from this machine, and the `Installation`, as it goes to the cluster.

The first `init` writes the installation's `id` into the file, so a cluster recreated from it is the same installation.

```bash
cat ~/.config/nereus/init.yaml
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: InitConfig
spec:
  profile: core
  ingressPort: 8080
  undercloud:
    create: false
    name: nereus
---
apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Installation
metadata:
  name: nereus
spec:
  alias: nereus
```

## InitConfig

Every key lives under `spec` of the `InitConfig` document.

| Key | Flag | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `profile` | `--profile` | `core` |
| `ingressPort` | `--ingress-port` | `8080` |
| `cloud` | `--target` | absent (`k3d`) |
| `undercloud.create` | `--create-cluster` | `false` |
| `undercloud.name` | `--name` | `nereus` |

`profile` is what `init` installs after core: `core` (nothing more), `internal-developer-platform` or `secrets` ([ADR 0014](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0014-profiles/), the profiles). A cloud target takes no profile yet.

`ingressPort` is the host port of the cluster's ingress gateway, from 1 to 65535, mapped on the loopback only to port 80 of the load balancer of a cluster `init` creates.

`cloud` names the Nereid of the cloud Reef whose cloud the cluster bootstraps. It is absent for a local `k3d` cluster, and it cannot be `k3d`.

`undercloud.create` creates the cluster, or reuses it when it exists. `undercloud.name` is the name of the cluster to create.

## Installation

The second document names the installation, after the cluster unless `--installation-name` says otherwise ([spec 0006](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0006-installation-identity/)).

| Key | Meaning | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `metadata.name` | The installation's name | `--installation-name` |
| `spec.alias` | The installation's alias | `init`, from the name |
| `spec.id` | The installation's UUID | the first `init` |
| `spec.naming.overrides` | Names that differ from the default | the author |

## Next

[Initialise the platform](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/) reads this file; the [Glossary](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/glossary/) holds the words.

# The installation

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/installation.md

Every installation has a name, an id and an alias, held by one `Installation` object in `nereus-system` that the first `nereus init` creates ([spec 0006](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0006-installation-identity/)).

See it with [`nereus config installation show`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#installation-show).

## Name

The object's name; it never changes. It prefixes every name the platform creates outside itself, such as the Azure resource group `<installation>-platform` ([spec 0005](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0005-cloud-reef/)).

It defaults to the cluster name; `--installation-name` sets another on the first `init`. A name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starts with a letter, at most 63 characters.

A second `init` with another name keeps the installation, and its `installation` line says `kept nereus-local, not acme-dev: the name of an installation never changes; another name is another installation`.

## Id

A random UUID; it never changes. Cloud resources can carry it, so they trace back to this installation. The API refuses a change, even by hand:

```bash
kubectl patch installations nereus-local \
  --namespace nereus-system \
  --type merge \
  --patch '{"spec":{"id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"}}'
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
The Installation "nereus-local" is invalid: spec.id: Invalid value: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000": the id of an installation never changes
```

The [settings file](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/settings/) also holds the id, so a cluster recreated from it is the same installation. A cluster recreated without it is a new installation with a new id.

## Alias

What listings show; free text, at most 63 characters, no control characters. It may change; the name and id stay, and the settings file follows: [`nereus config installation set --alias "Acme Prod"`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#installation-set).

## Address

`spec.url` is the address the API is published at: the chart's `ingress.address`, rewritten on every release, so it is not a setting. An instance with none (no Gateway, only port-forward) has no `url`.

`nereus status --output json` and `GET /v1/status` answer it as `installation.url`, `null` when absent. The portal's account sheet shows it with the `nereus login <url>` line.

## Naming overrides

When a generated cloud name is taken, a naming override sets it: `issuer.storage`, `state.storage` or `secrets.vault`, each checked against its resource's rules, with `nereus config installation set --naming-override issuer.storage=acmeissuers01`. See [A name is taken](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/troubleshoot/name-taken/).

## With Helm

The object belongs to the Helm release `nereus` and is kept on `helm uninstall`.

The chart creates it from `installation.name`, which it requires, and keeps the id and alias the cluster holds, so a plain `helm upgrade --install` gives the same identity as `init`.

Another name on the same cluster is refused, since the name never changes:

``` { .text .output title="output" }
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: execution error at (nereus/templates/installation.yaml:10:4): the installation of this cluster is nereus-local, not acme: the name of an installation never changes; another name is another installation
```

## One per namespace

A namespace holds one installation; a second is an error naming both. The undercloud and the overcloud are one installation: the pivot moves the object ([Undercloud and overcloud](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/undercloud-overcloud/)).

# What init does

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/init.md

What [`nereus init`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#init) does, step by step: the checks, the two Helm releases, the installation, the profile and the time. A first run is in [Prepare the cluster](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/init/).

## Prerequisites

`init` checks Docker (20.10.5 or newer, daemon running), k3d (5.0.0 or newer) and Helm (4.0.0 or newer) first. An older or missing one stops it before anything changes, naming the version it needs and where to get it.

Then it creates or reuses the local registry and the k3d cluster, and points the kube context at it. One registry serves every cluster `init` creates.

## Two Helm releases

From there `init` is two `helm upgrade --install`s and a wait ([#1055](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1055)), each a release of the same name in `nereus-system`; `helm list --namespace nereus-system` shows both.

- **`kinds`**: the chart `nereus-reefs` installs the `Reef`, `Nereid`, `Mandate`, `ServiceLevelObjective` and `Installation` kinds and the `nereus-system` namespace.
- **`nereus`**: the chart `nereus` installs the Nereus API with the values from the settings.
- **`installation`**: reads back the [installation](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/installation/) the chart created.

The kinds are templates, so every `helm upgrade` updates them; each is kept on `helm uninstall nereus-reefs`, with every object stored in it. [Install with Helm](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/helm/) installs the same charts without `init`.

## Core

The two charts also hold the profile core ([#1052](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1052)): the tenancy Reef's kinds and admission policy, the `Reef` tenancy and Nereus's own tree, the Organization `getnereus` with its Project `nereus` and four Projects under it.

All of it is kept on `helm uninstall`, since a person's own Projects hang from the tree ([Know whose each thing is](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/tenancy/)). On core alone, [`nereus status`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#status) lists `core` and `tenancy`, both `Ready`.

## The values file

`init` writes the values it passes to the chart `nereus` to `~/.config/nereus/values.yaml`, with the two `helm` commands that make the same install by hand in its header. `--dry-run` prints them and changes nothing.

``` { .text .output title="~/.config/nereus/values.yaml" }
image: localhost:5111/nereus-api:0.1.0-nereus-local
installation:
  name: nereus-local
  id: 1521c310-295d-49e9-a8ef-ed097f23fc46
  alias: nereus-local
profile: internal-developer-platform
thetis:
  image: localhost:5111/thetis-controller:0.1.0-nereus-local
  localRegistry: localhost:5111=k3d-nereus-registry.localhost:5000
nereids:
  registry: localhost:5111
  tag: 0.1.0-nereus-local
ingress:
  address: http://localhost:8080
```

## The images

The chart writes every Nereid's image into the `Profile`'s spec from `nereids`, and thetis installs them as written ([#1425](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1425)). A checkout's `init` takes them from the local registry, where `docker push localhost:5111/...` puts them.

A CLI installed from a release installs the charts published at its own version, `oci://ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus-reefs` and `.../nereus`, and the chart takes each image by digest from its `images.lock` ([#1785](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1785)).

`NEREUS_NEREIDS_REGISTRY` or `NEREUS_NEREIDS_TAG` wins over both: a cluster that cannot reach the local registry takes every image from the registry `make promote NEREUS_PROMOTE_TARGET=registry.example.com/team/nereus` copied them to ([Publish on ghcr.io](https://docs.getnereus.dev/agent/publish/)).

## Flux holds the releases

Once Flux `HelmRelease`s in `nereus-system` hold the releases `nereus-reefs` and `nereus`, Flux upgrades the charts with the `HelmRelease`'s values, and `init` leaves both alone:

``` { .text .output title="output" }
✓ kinds                     0.1s  release nereus-reefs held by HelmRelease nereus-reefs
✓ nereus                    0.0s  release nereus held by HelmRelease nereus
✓ installation              0.0s  kept nereus-local
✓ ready                     0.0s  the profile is HelmRelease nereus's
✓ public key                0.0s  the profile is HelmRelease nereus's
```

## The profile

`init` runs no step of the profile itself. The value `profile` makes the chart run [thetis](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/tree/main/controllers/thetis), the installer Nereid, which installs the profile's Reefs, Nereids and Mandates in order ([The profiles](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/profiles/)).

The step `ready` waits until each Nereid is Ready and prints how many and the slowest; each Nereid's time goes to the SLO report as a step of its own (`ready keycloak`).

The step `public key` prints the fingerprint of the secrets Reef's key.

## The time

Each step prints its time, and the total ends the run, even on failure (`✗`, then the error). On a terminal the lines are drawn live; elsewhere (CI, a script, a redirect, `NO_COLOR`) they print as each step ends ([#379](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/379)).

The total is measured against the target's SLO ([spec 0004](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0004-init-time-slo/)): green under 50%, yellow from 50%, orange from 75%, red past 100%. Missing it never stops `init`; `--check-slo` fails above it plus 10% ([Meet the time SLO](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/operate/slo/)).

## Run it again

[`nereus init --yes`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#init) again reuses the registry and the cluster, upgrades both releases with the same values (revision 2), keeps the installation's identity, and finds every Nereid Ready at once, in seconds and `0% green`.

# The profiles

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/profiles.md

The four built-in profiles, `core`, `internal-developer-platform`, `reference` and `secrets`, and what each installs. What a profile is: [Runtime install and profiles](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/runtime-and-profiles/).

## Choose one

[`nereus init --profile internal-developer-platform`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#init-profile) installs core, then the profile ([ADR 0014](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0014-profiles/), [#420](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/420)). An unknown profile is refused before anything changes:

``` { .text .output title="output" }
'minimal' is not a profile: core, internal-developer-platform, reference, secrets
```

[`nereus profile list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#profile-list) lists the four; `core` is the default. Profiles are built in; `profile create` is not built yet.

## core

No `--profile`, or `--profile core`, installs core alone with the tenancy Reef ([ADR 0015](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0015-tenancy/), [#646](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/646)): no other Reef, no Nereid.

## reference

`--profile reference` ([#1421](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1421)) installs the reference Nereid of each Reef that has one, such as `reference-secrets` ([#486](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/486)), in place of the tools: the Reefs' kinds answer end to end and no tool image is pulled. `make scene-core` runs it.

The authorization Reef's, `reference-authorization`, is the gate Nereid of [ADR 0031](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0031-gates-and-approvals/) there: a held object stays `Pending` until its Approval is decided ([#2213](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/2213)).

## internal-developer-platform

Each Nereid comes after the Nereids of the Reefs it requires. With this profile the instance offers sign-in, so `nereus status`, `reef` and `nereid` read through the Nereus API with your token.

- **Secrets:** Nereid `openbao`, Mandate `default` and the vault `default` ([Keep a secret](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/secrets/)).
- **Release:** Nereid `flux` and Mandate `flux` ([Release a chart](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/release/)).
- **Database:** Nereid `cloudnative-pg`, which installs CloudNativePG through a Release, and Mandate `cloudnative-pg`.
- **Authentication:** Nereid `keycloak`, its Database `keycloak` and Mandate `keycloak` ([Turn on authentication](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/authentication/)).
- **The entrance:** the Gateway API CRDs, Istio through the release Reef and the Gateway `istio-system/ingress` ([#951](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/951)).
- **Portal:** Nereid and Mandate `nereus-portal`, after the entrance ([#896](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/896)).
- **Metrics:** Nereid and Mandate `victoriametrics` ([Collect metrics](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/metrics/)).
- **Environment:** Nereid and Mandate `vcluster` ([#827](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/827)).
- **Catalog and delivery:** Nereids `catalog` and `kubernetes` ([Follow the golden path](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/golden-path/)).
- **Teams and authorization:** the `teams` Reef and Nereid `openfga` ([Say who may do what](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/access/authorization/)).
- **Registry:** Nereid `zot` ([Run a registry](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/registry/)).
- **Messaging:** Nereid `nats` and Mandate `messaging-nats` ([Send messages](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/messaging/)).
- **Build and scm:** Nereids `buildkit` and `forgejo`.
- **Usage and presentations:** Nereid `reference-usage` (the usage Reef's reference Nereid, until it has a real one) and Nereid `leagore`, so the portal shows the Usage and Presentations tabs ([#2018](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/2018)).

## The secrets Reef's key

OpenBao runs next to the Nereid `openbao`, which creates a non-exportable `rsa-4096` key and writes its public key in the Mandate's status; thetis checks it, and `init` prints its fingerprint.

The key lives on the volume `openbao-data` and OpenBao unseals itself, so a restarted Pod keeps it; only a lost volume makes a new key. The token and the unseal key are generated once, in Secrets, and never printed.

## The addresses on k3d

On k3d, `init` reads the ingress port from k3d and passes it as the chart's `ingress.address` ([#1079](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1079)). A new portal Mandate gets `publicUrl=http://localhost:<port>`, and the keycloak Mandate `http://auth.localhost:<port>` ([#1933](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1933)).

On another cluster `init` passes none, and the Mandates get no `publicUrl`; an existing Mandate is kept as it is. Set the portal's with `--param publicUrl=https://portal.example.com` on [`nereus mandate apply nereus-portal`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#mandate-apply).

A host no route names answers 404 from Envoy, and the portal answers on `localhost`:

```bash
curl --include --header "Host: no-route.example.com" http://localhost:8080/
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
server: istio-envoy
content-length: 0
```

## buildkit and forgejo

The profile installs `buildkit` in portable mode, Pod Security privileged, so it builds on any cluster. Where a sandbox runtime is installed, apply it in sandbox mode with `nereus nereid apply buildkit --set BUILD_RUNTIME_CLASS=gvisor` ([#1231](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1231)).

`forgejo` mirrors a repository through the scm Reef's default Mandate `forgejo` ([Mirror a repository](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/scm-mirror/)). Forgejo copies from github.com alone until `nereus nereid apply forgejo --set MIRROR_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=git.example.com` names other hosts.

## Apply a profile later

A profile also layers on core after `init` ([#425](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/425)): [`nereus profile apply internal-developer-platform`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#profile-apply) runs the same steps thetis runs, from the laptop, one line each, `created` the first time and `unchanged` after.

`--without buildkit` leaves a Nereid out; on a cluster the charts installed, the Profile's `spec.exclude` does the same. `--dry-run` lists the steps and changes nothing. On a cluster `init` has not prepared, it stops and points to `nereus init`.

## Describe a profile

[`nereus profile describe internal-developer-platform`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#profile-describe) shows its ingress and each Nereid with its Reef, Mandate and who requires it, in order.

The order comes from each Nereid's image label `core.getnereus.dev/requires` ([#1368](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1368)). With no registry answering, `describe` prints the order from the offline list `cli/src/nereus/requires.yaml`, and its last line says so.

## The proof

`make scene-idp` proves the profile ([#1261](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1261)): on a throwaway k3d cluster, every Nereid `Ready`, the portal answering, an app built by `buildkit` and deployed answering, and nothing left behind. It runs only on the owner's word ([#1420](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1420)).

# Reefs and Nereids

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs-and-nereids.md

The rules behind `nereus reef` and `nereus nereid`: what each command checks, writes and refuses. The model is in [Reef, Nereid and Mandate](https://docs.getnereus.dev/concepts/model/); a first run is in [Apply a Reef and its Nereid](https://docs.getnereus.dev/start/first-reef/).

## Apply a Reef

[`nereus reef apply release`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#reef-apply) applies the Reef's kinds from the version this CLI pins; applying again reports `unchanged` when no resourceVersion moved, as `kubectl apply` does.

[`nereus reef create release`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#reef-create) fails on an existing Reef, as `kubectl create` does, and shows the installed version: `reef cloud already exists (0.1.0)`.

`apply` takes three sources: the pinned version, local YAML with [`--from-file`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#reef-apply-file) (a file or a folder, alias `--path`), or a Reef package with `--image` (an OCI artifact of YAML layers). `--dry-run` lists what it would create.

With `--from-file`, it reports `configured` when the files changed a kind and `unchanged` when the same files come again.

## What a Reef may ship

A Reef is a `Reef` object, and may ship kinds of its own: the `cloud` Reef ships `Cloud` with the CLI, never with a Nereid ([spec 0005](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0005-cloud-reef/#the-objects)).

Whatever the source, the CLI checks every document first: only CustomResourceDefinitions of the platform's group, never a platform kind (`Reef`, `Nereid`, `Mandate`, `Installation`, `ServiceLevelObjective`), nor one another Reef owns.

A Reef may also ship a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` and binding, named `<name>.<reef group>`, matching only its own group, without parameters. The API then refuses for every client, as the tenancy Reef refuses a Project that is its own parent ([#646](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/646)).

## A Reef with no Nereid

The Reef's command group exists, empty until a Nereid is applied:

```bash
nereus release --help
```

``` { .text .output title="output" }
 Usage: nereus release [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

 Reef release: no Nereid applied.

 Apply one: nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef release --image <image>
```

[`nereus reef list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#reef-list) shows `-` under `NEREIDS`. Without the Reef, `nereid apply` is refused with `Apply it first: nereus reef apply release`.

## Apply a Nereid

[`nereus nereid apply reference-release`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-apply) reads the image's labels in the registry (manifest and config, no layer): name, Reef, required Reefs, version, repository.

It checks the Reef exists, writes the `Nereid` object pinned to the digest, runs the image as its controller and waits until it reports `Ready`. The same image again reports `core/nereids/reference-release unchanged`.

- A name argument wins over the label.
- `--reef <reef>` names a Reef the label lacks, or picks one when the label lists several; it repeats.
- An image that declares no Reef is refused: `declares no reef (label core.getnereus.dev/reef)`.

## The digest

The tag is resolved once to a digest (`pinned to`, the first 12 hex characters), so pushing the tag again never changes what runs.

An image given by digest (`--image <repository>@sha256:<64 hex>`) is applied as is, once its manifest matches. The full reference is in `spec.image`.

## Update a Nereid in place

[`nereus nereid apply reference-release --image`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-apply-image) moves a Nereid to another image with no delete: rules, Deployment and record move together; the apply ends once the new pod runs ([#386](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/386)).

`--dry-run` shows the digest it would move to. The same image with outdated rules names what it wrote, ending `clusterrole/controller-reference-release rules updated`.

A new image that fails prints the `nereus nereid apply` line with the last image that worked, which the Nereid records until a new pod has run.

Another Reef is refused: moving a Nereid between Reefs is a delete and an apply.

## List and get

[`nereus nereid list`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-list) shows each Nereid with its Reefs, image and status; [`nereus nereid get`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-get) adds the pinned digest, title, description and the Mandates naming it.

`reef list|get`, `nereid list|get` and `nereus status` read through the Nereus API with the token of `nereus login`, so they need no kubeconfig; only a member of `nereus-admins` reads them.

Logged out, they print `Not logged in` with the `nereus login` line. Until the instance offers sign-in (core alone), they read the cluster with the kubeconfig and print the same.

## Delete

[`nereus nereid delete reference-release`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#nereid-delete) removes the Nereid with its commands, Deployment, Service and identity, which belong to the `Nereid` object. The Reef stays, and its group says `no Nereid applied`.

`nereid delete` refuses the last Nereid of a Reef that applied Nereids require ([Require a Reef](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/build/requires/)), unless `--force`.

[`nereus reef delete release`](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/cli/core.html#reef-delete) removes the `Reef` object and keeps its kinds, so a Nereid's objects stay. It is refused while a Nereid of the Reef is applied, and names the `nereid delete` to run first.

## The objects

A Reef and a Nereid are Kubernetes objects, `Reef` and `Nereid` of `core.getnereus.dev`: `kubectl get reefs` and `kubectl get nereids` list them.

One writer per field (ADR 0005, one writer for each field of an object): the CLI writes the Reef and the Nereid's `spec.image`, `spec.reefs`, `spec.requires` and `spec.version`; the controller writes only `status.conditions` and `status.commands`.

The CLI caches each Reef's group and its Nereid's commands in `~/.cache/nereus/commands.json`, as `kubectl` caches API discovery; `reef` and `nereid` commands refresh it.

# Inside the metrics reef

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/metrics-reef.md

What the Nereid `victoriametrics` of the metrics Reef installs to keep the platform's metrics in [VictoriaMetrics](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/) (Apache-2.0) ([#742](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/742)). The queries are in [Collect metrics](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/metrics/).

## The operator

The Nereid asks the release Reef for the [VictoriaMetrics operator](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/operator/) (chart `victoria-metrics-operator` 0.68.1, operator v0.75.0, pinned by digest), released by the flux Mandate into the namespace `metrics-system`.

The operator turns a few Kubernetes kinds into running VictoriaMetrics components, as CloudNativePG turns a `Cluster` into PostgreSQL.

## VMSingle

One VictoriaMetrics server, `vmsingle-nereus` in `nereus-system`: it stores the samples on a 2Gi volume for 14 days and answers the Prometheus query API on port 8428. It also serves vmui, the web UI, at `/vmui`.

## VMAgent

The scraper, `vmagent-nereus`, reads the targets the Nereid's scrape objects name and writes the samples to the VMSingle with the Prometheus remote write protocol.

It reads only the scrape objects labelled with the Nereid's name, so another tool's objects never change what it collects.

It scrapes every 30s by default. The chart's `metrics.scrapeInterval` sets it: thetis writes it into the Mandate `victoriametrics` as the param `scrapeInterval` ([#2199](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/2199)).

The value is whole seconds from 10s to 60s, one value across the Nereid's Mandates. Any other value is refused by `nereus nereid apply`; the Nereid writes nothing and reports `InvalidScrapeInterval`.

The admission policy pins the VMAgent at the interval read at `nereus nereid apply`: after changing the param, apply the Nereid again.

## What it scrapes

The VMPodScrape `nereids` selects every pod labelled `core.getnereus.dev/metrics: "true"` in `nereus-system`, on its port `http` and path `/metrics`. Each Nereid built on nereid-sdk carries that label ([#741](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/741)), so no Nereid is ever named.

The label `nereid` of each series comes from the pod's `app.kubernetes.io/name`, never from what the pod serves, so no pod can pose as a Nereid.

The VMNodeScrape `kubelet-cadvisor` reads each node's kubelet at `/metrics/cadvisor`: CPU and memory per container. A target that fails shows as down, and nothing else stops.

The VMPodScrape `kube-state-metrics` reads [kube-state-metrics](https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics) ([#2177](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/2177)), which the Nereid also asks the release Reef for: chart 9.1.0, v2.20.0 pinned by digest, in `metrics-system`. The Nereid does not wait for it: it logs a Release not Ready.

It reads only pods, Deployments, ResourceQuotas and VerticalPodAutoscalers, through a Role in each namespace it reads, and no Secret. It exposes only the series the portal reads.

An Environment's health in the portal ([#2306](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/2306)): the nodes that answer, the pods pending, and the CPU and memory requested, of the namespace's ResourceQuota, else of the nodes' capacity.

It is under pressure when a pod is pending, a node does not answer or a meter passes 70%.

It reads `nereus-system` and each namespace a Ready Environment lists in `status.kubernetes.namespaces` ([#2305](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/2305)), but only one a Nereid made for a tenant ([#2348](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/2348)).

That is a Target's namespace, which the Nereid `flux` makes before its HelmRelease with the label `release.getnereus.dev/target`, or an Environment's `env-*`. A platform namespace such as `builds` never carries the label.

Kubernetes' own and the platform's namespaces are also refused by name, at the Nereid and at admission.

Only the Nereid serving the release Reef, or a cluster admin, may set, change or remove that label. A Target's namespace made before #2348, by Helm, has no label: a cluster admin adopts it once.

```bash
kubectl label namespace shop release.getnereus.dev/target=shop
```

Its one ClusterRole lists and watches the CustomResourceDefinitions, cluster-scoped: its Custom Resource State needs them to find the VPA's kind.

The Nereid also releases the [Vertical Pod Autoscaler](https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/tree/master/vertical-pod-autoscaler)'s recommender ([#2205](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/2205)): chart 0.17.0, VPA 1.8.1 pinned by digest, in `metrics-system`, with no updater and no webhook.

It writes one VerticalPodAutoscaler per Nereid Deployment, `updateMode: "Off"`: a CPU and a memory request are recommended, never applied. The recommender has a Role in `nereus-system` and no ClusterRole.

The recommender keeps the history in the VPA's checkpoints in `nereus-system`: a recommendation takes about 24 h after it starts and survives its restarts.

Its series keep their own `namespace` and `pod` (`honorLabels: true`): those of the pods they describe.

## The contract

The Mandate `victoriametrics` publishes `status.query.url`, the in-cluster address of the query API, `status.query.scrapeInterval` (`30s`) and its Ready condition; `nereus mandate get victoriametrics` shows them. It names no backend: another Nereid of the metrics Reef would publish the same fields.

The Nereus API keeps the status signals one scrape interval and steps the detail's 5m and 1h ranges by it.

## Who reaches it

The query API has no credentials yet. A NetworkPolicy, applied by `nereus nereid apply`, lets only the VMAgent and the Nereus API reach port 8428; a port-forward is not subject to it.

Deleting series takes a random key nobody is given (`-deleteAuthKey`, from the Secret `victoriametrics-delete-key`). An admission policy holds every object the Nereid writes to its name and its whole spec.

## The proof

`make scene-metrics` installs the Reef on a throwaway cluster and runs the three queries of [Collect metrics](https://docs.getnereus.dev/guides/reefs/metrics/), expecting one series per Nereid.

# What is built

Source: https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/what-is-built.md

What runs on `main` today, area by area, each with a status chip and where it is decided. [built]

Planned work and ideas are on the [roadmap](https://docs.getnereus.dev/project/roadmap/); each Reef's commands are in [the Reef pages](https://docs.getnereus.dev/reference/reefs/secrets/).

A chip says how far a feature is: `built` is code on `main`, `planned` has an issue that builds it, `idea` is still being refined.

## The CLI and the model

| Feature | What it gives | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `nereus init` | Prepares a cluster and installs nothing else; settings kept in a file. [ADR 0003](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0003-init-and-nereids-at-runtime/) | [built] |
| Time limit for `init` | A time SLO for `nereus init`, checked in CI. [spec 0004](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0004-init-time-slo/) | [built] |
| Installation identity | One `Installation` object per cluster, written by the first `init`. [spec 0006](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0006-installation-identity/) | [built] |
| Reefs at runtime | `nereus reef create | apply | list | delete`. [ADR 0010](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0010-reefs-at-runtime/) | [built] |
| Nereids at runtime | `nereus nereid apply` reads the image's labels from the registry. [ADR 0003](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0003-init-and-nereids-at-runtime/) | [built] |
| Required Reefs | A Nereid is refused when a Reef it requires is missing. [spec 0003](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0003-nereid-conformance/) | [built] |
| Commands from a Nereid | A Reef's command group is built from data in the Nereid's status. [ADR 0004](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0004-reefs-extend-the-cli/) | [built] |
| The CLI design commands | `reef`, `nereid`, `mandate` and the conventions. [ADR 0013](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0013-command-conventions/) | [built] |
| One writer per field | The CLI writes `spec`, a Nereid writes only `status`. [ADR 0005](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0005-one-writer-per-field/) | [built] |
| Profiles | `core` and `internal-developer-platform`; `nereus profile apply`. [ADR 0014](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0014-profiles/) | [built] |
| `nereus doctor` | Whether an instance is healthy, from `GET /v1/doctor`. [#799](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/799) | [built] |
| Swap checked in CI | Swapping a Nereid changes no command. [#124](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/124) | [built] |
| Untrusted Nereid output | What a Nereid publishes is untrusted input, with a test. [#134](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/134) | [built] |
| Nereid recovery | A Nereid that stops is reported and recovers by itself. [#133](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/133) | [built] |

## The Nereus API and MCP

| Feature | What it gives | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Nereus API | `nereus-api` in the cluster; `nereus whoami` calls `GET /v1/me`. [#607](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/607) | [built] |
| MCP tools from Reefs | A Reef declares tools; the API serves them at `/mcp`. [ADR 0029](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0029-mcp-tools/) | [built] |
| Chosen MCP tools | `nereus mcp tool enable | disable` in the `Installation`. [#1809](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1809) | [built] |
| `/mcp` in Claude Code | `nereus mcp client add claude-code`. [#1880](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1880) | [built] |
| `nereus-mcp` retired | The instance's entrance serves `/mcp`. [#1810](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1810) | [built] |

## Cloud and identity

| Feature | What it gives | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Reef kinds shipped by a Reef | The `cloud` Reef ships its kind `Cloud` and its Mandate. [spec 0005](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0005-cloud-reef/) | [built] |
| Cloud plans | A Nereid's plan is checked, approved and run with the person's login. [#307](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/307) | [built] |
| Requester tags | Every cloud resource says which installation created it and why. [#155](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/155) | [built] |
| Undercloud | `nereus init --target <name>` brings up the k3d undercloud. [#263](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/263) | [built] |
| Cloud grants | A Nereid that requires `cloud` is granted access by the person. [#310](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/310) | [built] |

## Reefs

| Feature | What it gives | Status |
|---|---|---|
| secrets | Vault and Secret, encrypted on the client. [#530](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/530) | [built] |
| release | Repository, Source, Target and Release. [ADR 0010](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0010-reefs-at-runtime/) | [built] |
| environment | An Environment per agent, with an expiry; the kept cluster `nereus`. [ADR 0026](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0026-environment-reef/) | [built] |
| catalog | `Workload`, `Package`, `WorkloadType` and `PackageType`. [ADR 0016](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0016-catalog-reef/) | [built] |
| database | A PostgreSQL per Database. [ADR 0017](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0017-resource-reefs/) | [built] |
| messaging | Topics and queues on NATS. [ADR 0019](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0019-messaging-reef/) | [built] |
| registry | Registry, Repository, publish and purge, with the `zot` Nereid. [ADR 0021](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0021-registry-reef/) | [built] |
| build | Builds of a Workload's source and Triggers on new commits. [spec 0009](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0009-build-security/) | [built] |
| scm | A GitHub App Mandate, a Forgejo `Mirror` and a one-hour `Token`. [ADR 0024](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0024-scm-reef/) | [built] |
| metrics | The `victoriametrics` Nereid. [#742](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/742) | [built] |
| ideas | The `doris` Nereid and Tide, its portal tab. [#1106](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1106) | [built] |
| portal | A PWA that says who you are. [spec 0008](https://docs.getnereus.dev/specs/0008-portal-first-slice/) | [built] |
| usage | A coding agent's quota window and its forecast. [#1590](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1590) | [built] |
| teams | `Team` and `Member` on the tenancy tree. [#1646](https://github.com/getnereus/nereus/issues/1646) | [built] |
| presentations | A deck kept by the platform and a Session to follow. [ADR 0028](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0028-presentations-reef/) | [built] |
| authorization | `Role` and `Binding`, asked before every read and write. [ADR 0027](https://docs.getnereus.dev/adr/0027-teams-roles-and-users/) | [built] |
